GA.name: Georgia Justice Project (GJP)
GA.what_they_offer: Provides legal assistance with record restriction and sealing (expungement), record corrections, First Offender issues, and pardons. Also offers free monthly virtual First Fridays information sessions, pro bono representation with volunteer defense attorneys, and online DIY record-clearing templates.
GA.who_qualifies: Individuals facing barriers to employment or housing due to a criminal history from arrests in Georgia; attending a First Fridays session is recommended before applying.
GA.cost: Free information sessions, DIY tools, and pro bono representation

GA.name: Middle Georgia Justice – Macon Judicial Circuit Second Opportunity Desk
GA.area_served: Bibb, Peach, Crawford, Houston, Monroe, Jones, and Twiggs Counties
GA.what_they_offer: Operates a bi-monthly help desk offering attorney criminal history reviews, consultations, self-help assistance, and representation for arrest record restrictions, court sealing petitions, and pardon applications.
GA.who_qualifies: Qualifying citizens of Bibb, Peach, Crawford, Houston, Monroe, Jones, and Twiggs Counties who pre-register and obtain their GCIC Code U and E reports.

GA.name: Cobb Second Chance Desk
GA.what_they_offer: Weekly help desk housed in the Cobb Circuit Defender's Office where an attorney reviews criminal histories, gives consultations, and helps fill out record restriction forms.
GA.who_qualifies: Individuals with eligible Cobb County criminal records who pre-register for an appointment.

GA.name: Augusta Judicial Circuit (AJC) Second Chance Desk
GA.what_they_offer: Monthly help desk at the Augusta Public Library offering attorney criminal record reviews, consultations, and self-help assistance filling out pro se restriction and sealing forms.
GA.who_qualifies: Citizens with eligible criminal records stemming from arrests or cases in Burke and Richmond Counties.

GA.name: Athens-Clarke County Second Chance Desk
GA.what_they_offer: Monthly help desk providing attorney reviews of criminal histories, consultations, and assistance completing pro se restriction and sealing forms.
GA.who_qualifies: Residents with eligible criminal records from arrests or cases in Athens-Clarke and Oconee Counties.

GA.name: GeorgiaLegalAid.org
GA.what_they_offer: Provides online self-help legal guides and an automated virtual assistant chatbot explaining how to review GCIC reports, restrict and seal records, use Retroactive First Offender laws, and seek pardons.

SD.name: South Dakota Unified Judicial System (UJS) Self-Help
SD.what_they_offer: Provides an online Guide and File system that generates completed expungement paperwork, printable pro se expungement forms and instructions, and a Legal Form Help Line to answer questions about filling out forms.
SD.who_qualifies: Self-represented individuals seeking to expunge eligible arrest records after an acquittal, dismissal, or uncharged arrest.

SD.name: East River Legal Services
SD.what_they_offer: Provides free civil legal services, including assistance with criminal record expungement and overcoming reentry barriers.
SD.who_qualifies: Low-income residents in eastern South Dakota, generally with income at or below 125% of the federal poverty level (up to 200% for certain case types).

SD.name: Dakota Plains Legal Services
SD.area_served: 33 counties in central and western South Dakota and all reservations in South Dakota
SD.what_they_offer: Offers free civil and tribal legal aid, including assistance with expungement documents, civil matters connected to criminal records, and mobile Justice Bus services.
SD.who_qualifies: Income-eligible low-income and Native American residents within its service area.

RI.name: Justice Assistance
RI.what_they_offer: Hosts monthly in-person expungement clinics in Cranston by appointment in partnership with the Office of the Rhode Island Public Defender to help clear eligible criminal records.

RI.name: Office of the Rhode Island Public Defender
RI.what_they_offer: Provides an online resource guide on expunging and sealing criminal records, co-hosts free monthly expungement clinics with Justice Assistance, and offers direct expungement outreach assistance.
RI.who_qualifies: Direct assistance from the Community Outreach Liaison is for current or former clients of the Rhode Island Public Defender, and monthly clinics are available by appointment.

RI.name: Rhode Island Legal Services
RI.what_they_offer: Assists with expungement, sealing, and correction of criminal records from offices in Providence and Newport, including through its Removing Barriers to Employment program.
RI.who_qualifies: People who were not clients of the Rhode Island Public Defender and are unable to hire a lawyer.

RI.name: Operation Stand Down Rhode Island
RI.what_they_offer: Provides record review, evaluation, and legal expungement services to help clear criminal records.

RI.name: OpenDoors
RI.what_they_offer: Checks expungement and record sealing eligibility online or at weekly walk-in clinics at 485 Plainfield, and prepares motion-to-expunge forms with case details filled in.

RI.name: Rhode Island Office of the Attorney General
RI.what_they_offer: Helps residents evaluate criminal record expungement eligibility and complete forms through community outreach hours and periodic clinics, though online expungement requests are not currently accepted.

OR.name: CLEAR Clinic
OR.what_they_offer: Provides limited-scope legal help and weekly drop-in clinics for criminal and eviction record expungements, court fine and fee waivers, and SB 819 felony relief applications. Services are offered across the Portland metro area, at Oregon prisons, at tribal nations, and around the state.
OR.who_qualifies: People with a criminal record; no appointment or advance intake form is needed for walk-in clinics.

OR.name: Legal Aid Services of Oregon - Expungement Clinic
OR.what_they_offer: Offers statewide remote assistance as well as in-person clinics in Gresham, Multnomah County, and Clackamas County. Attorneys review criminal and eviction records to check eligibility and complete necessary court paperwork.
OR.who_qualifies: Low-income Oregonians with incomes up to 125% of the federal poverty level, or slightly above in some situations.

OR.name: Clean Slate Clackamas
OR.what_they_offer: Hosts monthly legal clinics in Milwaukie in partnership with the CLEAR Clinic and Clackamas County Children, Family & Community Connections. Helps participants with Oregon circuit court criminal and eviction record expungements and court fee waivers.
OR.who_qualifies: Open to everyone in the Clackamas County area with eligible Oregon county circuit court records.
OR.cost: Free legal services (filing fees may apply)

OR.name: Mid-Willamette Valley Community Action - Reentry Services Expungement Clinic
OR.what_they_offer: Hosts a monthly walk-in expungement clinic in Salem in partnership with the Public Defender of Marion County to help clear past Oregon criminal records.
OR.who_qualifies: Anyone with an eligible Oregon criminal record who meets the waiting periods and has no open cases or active warrants.
OR.cost: Free clinic ($33 fee for required fingerprinting)

OR.name: Columbia River Gorge Criminal Records Expungement Clinic
OR.area_served: Wasco, Hood River, Gilliam, Sherman, Umatilla, Wheeler, Baker, and Morrow Counties
OR.what_they_offer: Volunteer lawyers and trained volunteers hold monthly walk-in clinics in Hood River and The Dalles in collaboration with the CLEAR Clinic. They review Oregon criminal records, prepare expungement paperwork, and take required fingerprints.
OR.who_qualifies: People with an Oregon criminal record; walk-ins are welcome without an appointment.

OR.name: Youth, Rights & Justice
OR.what_they_offer: Nonprofit law firm partnering with Lewis & Clark Law School's Criminal Justice Reform Clinic to provide juvenile record expungement services.
OR.who_qualifies: Juveniles with criminal records in Multnomah, Washington, and Clackamas Counties.

OR.name: Lewis & Clark Law School - Criminal Justice Reform Clinic
OR.what_they_offer: Partners with Youth, Rights & Justice to provide juvenile record expungements, and works with Metropolitan Public Defender on representing clients in municipal and circuit courts for expungements.
OR.who_qualifies: Juveniles with criminal records in Multnomah, Washington, and Clackamas Counties, as well as clients referred through its Barrier Reduction Project.

AZ.name: Arizona Democracy Resource Center - Free Legal Clinic
AZ.what_they_offer: Provides one-on-one legal support, petition preparation and filing, and hearing assistance for record sealing, set-asides, Certificates of Second Chance, marijuana expungement, Class 6 felony reclassification, and civil rights restoration.
AZ.who_qualifies: Anyone with an eligible Arizona criminal record who has completed applicable sentence terms such as probation and restitution.

AZ.name: FREE Arizona
AZ.what_they_offer: Offers petition services for Proposition 207 marijuana expungements, help applying to reduce Class 6 undesignated felonies to misdemeanors, end-to-end civil rights restoration assistance, and set-aside guidance.
AZ.who_qualifies: Individuals impacted by the criminal system, including those with qualifying marijuana offenses before November 30, 2020 or completed supervision on a Class 6 undesignated felony.

AZ.name: Defenders of Children
AZ.what_they_offer: Provides legal assistance to set aside and expunge criminal records, restore civil rights, and resolve related employment, housing, and education civil legal issues.

AZ.name: University of Arizona College of Law - Civil Rights Restoration Clinic
AZ.what_they_offer: Law students and clinic staff evaluate eligibility, prepare court pleadings, and represent clients in court to set aside convictions, restore civil rights, and expunge marijuana records under Proposition 207.
AZ.who_qualifies: Persons previously convicted of criminal offenses, including individuals eligible for Proposition 207 marijuana expungement.

AZ.name: Sandra Day O'Connor College of Law Post-Conviction Clinic (Arizona State University)
AZ.what_they_offer: Evaluates cases for suitability, helps individuals fill out court paperwork, and litigates contested cases to expunge marijuana charges under Proposition 207.
AZ.who_qualifies: People convicted of eligible state marijuana offenses such as possession of 2.5 ounces or less or up to six plants at a residence, excluding federal convictions.

AZ.name: Arizona Judicial Branch Self-Service Center
AZ.what_they_offer: Provides self-help legal information and criminal court forms for sealing criminal case records, setting aside convictions, restoring civil rights, designating Class 6 felonies as misdemeanors, and expunging marijuana charges.
AZ.who_qualifies: Individuals arrested, convicted, or sentenced in Arizona who meet specific statutory requirements.

AZ.name: Arizona Reentry 2030
AZ.what_they_offer: State initiative offering information on Arizona record clearance laws, a free online record-sealing eligibility screening tool in partnership with Rasa Legal, and directory links to free legal aid organizations.
AZ.who_qualifies: All Arizonans with criminal records can access the eligibility screening tool.

AZ.name: Pima County Public Defense Services Legal Clinic
AZ.what_they_offer: Accepts requests for legal clinic assistance through an online form for individuals seeking rights restoration and record-clearing help.

OH.name: Opportunity Port (The Ohio State University Moritz College of Law)
OH.what_they_offer: Online intake program that determines record clearing eligibility and connects users with partner legal providers by phone and email to prepare Ohio sealing or expungement applications.
OH.who_qualifies: Franklin County residents seeking to seal or expunge an Ohio arrest, dismissal, or conviction (services outside Franklin County are paused until further notice); some partner providers have income requirements.

OH.name: Franklin County Municipal Court Self Help Resource Center
OH.what_they_offer: Participates as an Opportunity Port service provider to help applicants complete criminal record sealing and expungement paperwork by phone and email.
OH.who_qualifies: Individuals applying through Opportunity Port to seal or expunge an arrest, dismissal, or conviction in Ohio; some providers have income limits.

OH.name: Equality Ohio
OH.what_they_offer: Serves as an Opportunity Port partner organization providing phone appointments and completed applications for sealing or expunging Ohio criminal records.
OH.who_qualifies: Users seeking to seal or expunge an Ohio arrest, dismissal, or conviction through Opportunity Port; some providers have income limits.

OH.name: Legal Aid of Southeast and Central Ohio (LASCO)
OH.area_served: Southeast and Central Ohio (including Franklin, Tuscarawas, and Pickaway Counties)
OH.what_they_offer: Offers Fresh Start record sealing clinics and serves as an Opportunity Port provider to screen individuals for eligibility and help complete sealing or expungement paperwork.
OH.who_qualifies: Individuals meeting eligibility and income guidelines (generally under 200% of the federal poverty guideline) who do not have open cases and are not currently on probation or community control.

OH.name: Community Legal Aid
OH.what_they_offer: Hosts a monthly online clinic where volunteer attorneys advise clients and help prepare court forms for self-representation in sealing or expungement cases, plus walk-in legal information sessions at the Akron-Canton Regional Food Bank.
OH.who_qualifies: Legal aid eligible clients; advance registration is required for the monthly online clinic.

OH.name: University of Akron School of Law - Reentry Clinic
OH.area_served: City of Akron and Summit County
OH.what_they_offer: Supervised law students and volunteer lawyers conduct background searches, assist with applications for record sealing, expungement, Certificates of Qualification for Employment (CQE), clemency, and license restoration, and represent clients in court.
OH.who_qualifies: Low-income residents of the City of Akron, or Summit County residents who have a minor child residing in Summit County.

OH.name: Summit County Pro Bono Collaborative
OH.what_they_offer: Runs a clinic on the first Friday of the month at the Summit County Courthouse offering assistance with expungements, driver's license suspensions, and other civil legal matters.

OH.name: Summit Legal Defenders - Clean Slate Program
OH.what_they_offer: Provides assistance with sealing and expunging adult and juvenile criminal records in Summit County, specialty expungement for human trafficking victims, resolving warrants, and reinstating driving privileges.
OH.who_qualifies: Individuals with criminal convictions or juvenile records within Summit County, including victims of human trafficking.

OH.name: The Legal Aid Society of Cleveland
OH.what_they_offer: Accepts record clearing applications daily and hosts virtual clinics where volunteer attorneys assess eligibility, review and correct paperwork, and mail ready-to-file documents with instructions.

OH.name: LegalWorks
OH.what_they_offer: Holds weekly walk-in and appointment office hours and clinics across Cleveland to assist with motions to seal and expunge records, governor's pardon eligibility, arrest warrants, and license suspensions.
OH.who_qualifies: Individuals with past criminal records or legal issues in Cuyahoga and adjacent counties.
OH.cost: Free weekly office hours; free and low-cost legal services

OH.name: Ohio Legal Help
OH.what_they_offer: Provides an online self-help interview that checks whether individual Ohio charges qualify for sealing or expungement and creates a customized action plan with filing instructions.
OH.who_qualifies: Anyone looking to check eligibility to seal or expunge an Ohio criminal record.

OH.name: Toledo Bar Association Pro Bono Legal Services Program
OH.what_they_offer: Holds a monthly Criminal Record Sealing Clinic by appointment where volunteer attorneys provide individual help preparing record sealing and expungement filings.
OH.who_qualifies: Low-income Lucas County residents who cannot afford an attorney and meet Legal Aid screening guidelines.

OH.name: Cuyahoga County Office of the Public Defender
OH.what_they_offer: Represents individuals applying to seal or expunge adult felony records in the Cuyahoga County Common Pleas Court.
OH.who_qualifies: Individuals seeking to seal or expunge adult felony records in Cuyahoga County Common Pleas Court (requires an application and financial disclosure form).

OH.name: Cleveland State University College of Law - Pardon, Clemency, and Reentry Clinic
OH.what_they_offer: Supervised law students represent clients in municipal and county courts to seek record sealing, expungement, governor's pardons or clemency, and post-conviction relief.
OH.who_qualifies: Indigent individuals in Northeast Ohio with criminal convictions.

OH.name: Case Western Reserve University School of Law - Second Chance Reentry Clinic
OH.what_they_offer: Law school clinic assisting with criminal record sealing and expungement, Certificates of Qualification for Employment, and relief from weapons disability.

VA.name: Legal Aid Justice Center
VA.area_served: Charlottesville area (Albemarle, Charlottesville, Fluvanna), Northern Virginia, Richmond, Petersburg, and Hampton/Newport News
VA.what_they_offer: Provides free legal assistance to remove old arrests and non-convictions from criminal records, advises on eligibility under the new record sealing law, and hosts local expungement clinics.
VA.who_qualifies: Financially eligible people living in or with legal issues arising in their service areas.

VA.name: Legal Aid Society of Eastern Virginia (LASEV)
VA.what_they_offer: Hosts criminal records expungement clinics where participants receive legal advice from attorneys, and accepts general applications for free civil legal services by phone.
VA.who_qualifies: Low-income residents of Hampton Roads; specific community clinics are for NRHA public housing residents, while non-residents can apply for services by phone.

VA.name: Regent University Center for Global Justice Clinic
VA.what_they_offer: Provides free legal representation to help survivors of human trafficking petition to vacate or expunge eligible criminal charges and convictions from their records.
VA.who_qualifies: Survivors of sex or labor trafficking with qualifying Virginia misdemeanor or nonviolent felony convictions.

VA.name: Virginia Free Legal Answers (VA FLA)
VA.what_they_offer: Operates an online pro bono Q&A platform where users can ask questions by email to check their record sealing eligibility and receive legal advice.

VA.name: Virginia Lawyer Referral Service (VLRS)
VA.what_they_offer: Connects callers with an attorney for a free 30-minute consultation on record sealing eligibility and legal questions, and provides referrals if paid representation is needed.
VA.cost: Free 30-minute consultation ($35 referral fee waived for record sealing through June 30, 2027); ongoing representation is paid.

VA.name: Virginia Law Help
VA.what_they_offer: Publishes upcoming expungement clinic events and connects residents through the statewide legal aid hotline to local legal aid offices that may offer record clearing help.
VA.who_qualifies: Low-income individuals who qualify based on income.

VA.name: Virginia Legal Aid Society (VLAS)
VA.what_they_offer: Provides online self-help legal information on expungement and record sealing and may offer legal assistance in those areas through its intake line.

VA.name: Virginia Indigent Defense Commission (VIDC)
VA.what_they_offer: Provides public expungement overview guides, links to official court petition forms, online record sealing resources, group trainings, and a dedicated resource attorney.

VA.name: Virginia State Crime Commission
VA.what_they_offer: Provides official guides, FAQs, brochures, lists of eligible and excluded offenses, and links to request criminal history records and search court cases for record sealing.

DC.name: Rising for Justice (formerly D.C. Law Students in Court)
DC.what_they_offer: Provides free eligibility determinations, intake interviews, and attorney representation to file record sealing motions and handle court hearings through resolution. Clients may also be referred to their Social Work Program.
DC.who_qualifies: Eligible indigent or low-income residents in Washington, DC.

DC.name: Legal Aid Society of the District of Columbia
DC.what_they_offer: Provides direct legal help and representation for criminal record sealing and expungement cases in the District of Columbia.
DC.who_qualifies: Individuals with DC legal matters whose household income is generally at or below 200% (and up to 300% for some cases) of the Federal Poverty Guidelines.

DC.name: Christian Legal Aid of DC (CLADC)
DC.what_they_offer: Reviews criminal records for eligibility and connects eligible clients with an attorney to file Motions to Seal and Motions to Set Aside under the Youth Rehabilitation Act.
DC.who_qualifies: Clients with a DC legal matter whose income does not exceed HUD's Low (80%) Income Limits.

DC.name: Neighborhood Legal Services Program (NLSP)
DC.what_they_offer: Offers legal advice, walk-in clinics, and attorney assistance with drafting and filing motions to seal and expunge DC criminal records that create barriers to employment.
DC.who_qualifies: Individuals who pass an eligibility check with an NLSP intake specialist.

DC.name: D.C. Bar Pro Bono Center
DC.what_they_offer: Offers walk-in consultations on criminal record sealing and expungement at its Advice & Referral Clinic, and matches eligible residents with partner organizations or pro bono attorneys.

DC.name: Public Defender Service for the District of Columbia (PDS)
DC.what_they_offer: Provides free legal representation for record sealing, runs regular expungement clinics through its Community Defender Division, and publishes the D.C. Reentry Navigator self-help manual and sample motions.
DC.who_qualifies: Primarily DC residents represented by PDS or appointed counsel in their original cases, though the Community Defender Division serves residents more broadly.

DC.name: Catholic Charities Legal Network
DC.what_they_offer: Listed by the District of Columbia Courts as a legal services provider handling criminal record sealing matters.

WI.name: Legal Action of Wisconsin
WI.what_they_offer: Provides legal representation and community clinics for expungements, pardons, arrest record corrections, and criminal background check cleanup.

WI.name: Urban League of Greater Madison
WI.what_they_offer: Hosts monthly legal expungement clinics in partnership with Legal Action of Wisconsin and volunteer attorneys to review criminal records, advise on expungement, arrest removal, and pardons, and help file court paperwork if eligible.
WI.who_qualifies: Dane County residents who pre-register for a clinic.

WI.name: Milwaukee Justice Center Expungement & Pardon Clinic
WI.what_they_offer: Volunteer attorneys and law students offer confidential brief legal advice, eligibility assessments, referrals, and virtual pardon application appointments for Wisconsin convictions (on break from August through December 2026).
WI.who_qualifies: Low-income self-represented individuals; pardon appointments require establishing eligibility by email or phone first.

WI.name: LIFT Wisconsin
WI.what_they_offer: Provides the online Legal Tune Up tool at legaltuneup.org and legal clinics to help people check public data and remove eligible criminal and eviction records.
WI.who_qualifies: Low-income Wisconsin residents, with no application required to attend a clinic or use the online tool.

WI.name: LOTUS Legal Clinic
WI.what_they_offer: Provides legal counsel in English and Spanish for expungements and pardons for trafficking and gender-based violence survivors.
WI.who_qualifies: Survivors of gender-based violence and human trafficking, regardless of income.

WI.name: Lawyers for Learners
WI.what_they_offer: Connects college students with virtual or in-person legal assistance for expungements, pardons, and criminal background and arrest records from civil and municipal court proceedings.
WI.who_qualifies: Students and prospective students at partner colleges across Wisconsin.

WI.name: Sherman Park Community Association
WI.what_they_offer: Hosts bi-weekly drop-in legal office hours in partnership with Legal Action of Wisconsin to assist residents with expungements, pardons, and other civil legal issues.
WI.who_qualifies: Sherman Park residents living in the 53210 and 53216 zip codes.

ID.name: Idaho Supreme Court
ID.what_they_offer: Provides official self-help instructions and court petition forms to shield eligible criminal records from public view under the Clean Slate Act, as well as forms to vacate and seal alcohol age violations.
ID.who_qualifies: People with one eligible offense or set of offenses from a single incident who completed their full sentence, including probation, parole, fines, and restitution, at least 5 years ago.

ID.name: Idaho State Police, Bureau of Criminal Identification
ID.what_they_offer: Provides an official expungement application and flow chart, and processes written requests to expunge fingerprints and non-conviction arrest records from the state criminal history repository.
ID.who_qualifies: Anyone arrested or served a criminal summons in Idaho who was not charged within one year, had all charges dismissed, or was acquitted of all offenses.

MN.name: Volunteer Lawyers Network (VLN)
MN.what_they_offer: Provides phone-based legal advice, brief services, full representation for criminal expungement cases, and criminal records workshops.
MN.who_qualifies: Low-income people in Minnesota who meet income qualifications.

MN.name: Central Minnesota Legal Services (CMLS)
MN.area_served: Anoka, Benton, Big Stone, Chippewa, Chisago, Hennepin, Isanti, Kandiyohi, Lac Qui Parle, Lincoln, Lyon, Meeker, Mille Lacs, Morrison, Renville, Sherburne, Stearns, Swift, Todd, Wright, and Yellow Medicine Counties
MN.what_they_offer: Provides legal advice, brief services, and full representation in select criminal expungement cases.
MN.who_qualifies: Low-income people in the service area.

MN.name: Justice North
MN.area_served: Aitkin, Becker, Beltrami, Carlton, Cass, Clay, Clearwater, Cook, Crow Wing, Douglas, Grant, Hubbard, Itasca, Kanabec, Kittson, Koochiching, Lake, Lake of the Woods, Mahnomen, Marshall, Norman, Otter Tail, Pennington, Pine, Polk, Pope, Red Lake, Roseau, St. Louis, Stevens, Traverse, Wadena, and Wilkin Counties
MN.what_they_offer: Provides legal advice, brief services, and full representation in select criminal expungement cases.

MN.name: Southern Minnesota Regional Legal Services (SMRLS)
MN.area_served: Blue Earth, Brown, Carver, Cottonwood, Dakota, Dodge, Faribault, Fillmore, Freeborn, Goodhue, Houston, Jackson, Le Sueur, Martin, McLeod, Mower, Murray, Nicollet, Nobles, Olmsted, Pipestone, Ramsey, Redwood, Rice, Rock, Scott, Sibley, Steele, Wabasha, Waseca, Washington, Watonwan, and Winona Counties
MN.what_they_offer: Works individually with clients at criminal expungement clinics to draft, serve, and file expungement petitions, without providing court representation.
MN.who_qualifies: Income-eligible residents who have an appointment.

MN.name: Legal Assistance of Olmsted County (LAOC) - Criminal Expungement Clinic
MN.what_they_offer: Holds bi-monthly remote telephone clinics offering brief advice consultations with volunteer criminal defense lawyers on whether criminal expungement is a viable option.
MN.who_qualifies: Self-represented individuals who register in advance through the Olmsted County Law Library.

MN.name: Neighborhood Justice Center (NJC)
MN.what_they_offer: Offers attorney consultations and legal representation for criminal expungements.
MN.who_qualifies: Residents or individuals seeking an expungement in Ramsey, Dakota, or Washington Counties.

MN.name: Mitchell Hamline School of Law Clinics
MN.what_they_offer: Operates a Re-Entry Clinic for sealing criminal records, a Pro Se Self-Help Clinic for expungement, and the LAMP Clinic to help incarcerated individuals seek pardons or sentence commutations.
MN.who_qualifies: The Re-Entry Clinic serves only people who have served prison time, and the LAMP Clinic serves incarcerated individuals.

MN.name: Hennepin County Attorney's Office - Prosecutor-Led Expungement (PLE) Program
MN.what_they_offer: Reviews and seals eligible conviction records directly on the applicant's behalf without requiring court filings or court appearances.
MN.who_qualifies: People convicted of eligible offenses prosecuted by the Hennepin County Attorney's Office who have completed probation or parole and satisfied the required waiting period without new convictions.

MN.name: Anoka County Criminal Expungement Clinic
MN.what_they_offer: Holds monthly walk-in informational sessions on criminal expungement, supplies court forms, and provides attorney consultations supported by Central Minnesota Legal Services.
MN.who_qualifies: Participants must attend the clinic presentation and financially qualify to speak with an attorney.

MN.name: Ramsey County Law Library - Criminal Expungement Clinic
MN.what_they_offer: Provides a monthly in-person clinic explaining the criminal expungement process and offering attorney help with completing expungement forms.
MN.who_qualifies: Anyone filing an expungement for a criminal case in Ramsey County.

MN.name: Washington County Law Library - Criminal Legal Advice Clinic
MN.what_they_offer: Holds weekly legal advice clinics providing a 30-minute attorney consultation on criminal expungement and other criminal or traffic issues.
MN.who_qualifies: Washington County residents of modest means.

MN.name: Statewide Minnesota Judicial Branch Self-Help Centers
MN.what_they_offer: Provides self-help information, criminal expungement forms, and courthouse workstations to assist self-represented litigants.
MN.who_qualifies: People representing themselves in the Minnesota District Courts.

TN.name: West Tennessee Legal Services
TN.area_served: 21 counties in West Tennessee, including Memphis
TN.what_they_offer: Provides legal advice and representation for expunging eligible charges and convictions, restoring voting and citizenship rights, and reinstating driver's licenses.

TN.name: Legal Aid Society of Middle Tennessee and the Cumberlands
TN.area_served: Middle Tennessee and the Cumberlands, including Nashville, Sumner County, Montgomery, Stewart, Robertson, Houston, Dickson, Cheatham, and Humphreys counties
TN.what_they_offer: Reviews criminal records to advise which charges can be expunged, assists with restoration of rights, and hosts free expungement clinics.
TN.who_qualifies: Individuals experiencing low income and vulnerable individuals, including people age 55 and older.

TN.name: University of Tennessee Winston College of Law Legal Clinic
TN.area_served: Knox County and East Tennessee, including Monroe, Polk, and Jefferson counties
TN.what_they_offer: Law students supervised by faculty assist clients with analyzing criminal records, requesting court cost waivers, and filing expungement petitions, as well as running an expungement hotline and community clinics.
TN.who_qualifies: Clients who cannot afford an attorney.

TN.name: University of Memphis School of Law Expungement and Restoration of Rights Clinic
TN.what_they_offer: Law students supervised by licensed faculty provide direct representation for criminal record expungements, court cost waivers in closed criminal matters, restoration of citizenship and voting rights, and certificates of employability.

TN.name: Vanderbilt Law School Community Justice Legal Project
TN.what_they_offer: Law students and a supervising attorney hold monthly workshops and one-on-one sessions at the McGruder Family Resource Center offering limited-scope advice on expungements, driver's license restoration, and voting rights.
TN.who_qualifies: Community members facing civil legal barriers after involvement with the justice system.

TN.name: Lincoln Memorial University Duncan School of Law Expungement Pro Bono Project
TN.what_they_offer: Assists residents with analyzing criminal records, requesting court cost waivers, and petitioning for dismissal and conviction expungements.

TN.name: Knox County District Attorney's Office
TN.what_they_offer: Holds monthly in-person expungement screenings with an Assistant District Attorney and a court clerk to assist self-represented individuals with expungement applications, eligibility questions, and rights restoration.
TN.who_qualifies: Pro se defendants with eligible Knox County criminal cases.
TN.cost: Free for dismissals and not guilty verdicts; $100 court clerk fee for diversions and convictions

TN.name: Knox County Public Defender's Office
TN.what_they_offer: Provides expungement assistance to former clients.
TN.who_qualifies: Individuals who were represented by the Knox County Public Defender's Office.

TN.name: General Sessions Court of Metropolitan Nashville & Davidson County (Division VIII)
TN.what_they_offer: Hosts Saturday expungement and legal clinics with volunteer pro bono attorneys alongside an indigency docket and resource fair.
TN.who_qualifies: Limited to the first 100 registrants; indigency docket registrants must be interviewed by the Criminal Court Clerk Office.

TN.name: Vet to Vet Tennessee
TN.area_served: Monroe County, Polk County, and East Tennessee
TN.what_they_offer: Partners with the University of Tennessee College of Law and local judges to sponsor community expungement clinics.

TN.name: TN Free Legal Answers
TN.what_they_offer: Online service where volunteer attorneys answer non-criminal legal questions at no cost, featured alongside self-help expungement forms and instructions.
TN.who_qualifies: People in Tennessee who cannot afford a lawyer and meet online eligibility requirements.

CA.name: Community Legal Aid SoCal
CA.area_served: Orange and Los Angeles Counties (and clinics open to Riverside and San Bernardino County residents)
CA.what_they_offer: Provides legal assistance and monthly clinics for criminal record analysis, expungements, record sealing, driver's license restoration, and overcoming employment or licensing barriers.
CA.who_qualifies: Orange and Los Angeles County residents with eligible California criminal records, or non-residents with eligible criminal records in Orange or Los Angeles County.

CA.name: Legal Aid Foundation of Los Angeles (LAFLA)
CA.what_they_offer: Offers legal services, clinics, and self-help guides to clear criminal records through expungement and Prop 47 petitions, as well as assistance with Fair Chance Hiring violations.
CA.who_qualifies: Eligible individuals facing criminal record barriers to gainful employment.

CA.name: Central California Legal Services (CCLS)
CA.area_served: Fresno, Merced, Visalia, Mendota, and Los Banos
CA.what_they_offer: Staff and volunteer lawyers assess expungement eligibility, prepare court forms, help draft personal statements, gather supporting evidence, and prepare clients for court hearings.
CA.who_qualifies: Individuals with an eligible conviction in California who apply and qualify for services.

CA.name: LASSB
CA.what_they_offer: Provides telephone and in-person expungement clinic assistance for expungements, Prop 47 petitions, reducing infractions or traffic offenses, and early termination applications.
CA.who_qualifies: Eligible individuals determined by available resources and legal aid priorities.

CA.name: Inland Empire Latino Lawyers Association, Inc. (IELLA)
CA.what_they_offer: Offers limited-scope legal clinics where volunteer attorneys and staff review criminal records, provide legal advice, and prepare expungement petitions for clients to file.
CA.who_qualifies: Low-income residents of the Inland Empire with eligible criminal convictions.

CA.name: East Bay Community Law Center (EBCLC) - Clean Slate Clinic
CA.what_they_offer: Attorneys and advocates help with post-conviction remedies, factual innocence arrest record sealing, vacating convictions for human trafficking survivors and immigrants, and employment or licensing denials.
CA.who_qualifies: Individuals seeking remedies for arrests or convictions in Alameda County who face barriers to employment or occupational licensure due to a criminal record.

CA.name: Inland Counties Legal Services, Inc. (ICLS) - Expungement Clinic
CA.what_they_offer: Guides individuals through the record-clearing process and assists with filing expungement forms with the court.
CA.who_qualifies: Adults convicted of eligible misdemeanor or felony charges in Riverside or San Bernardino County who meet ICLS eligibility requirements (excludes juvenile charges, sex crimes involving a minor, sidewalk vending, and traffic tickets).

CA.name: San Francisco Public Defender - Clean Slate Program
CA.what_they_offer: Reviews RAP sheets and assists with clearing or reducing arrests and convictions, obtaining Certificates of Rehabilitation, and terminating Tier 1 or Tier 2 PC 290 registration.
CA.who_qualifies: Individuals who cannot afford an attorney and whose arrest, conviction, or court-transferred probation occurred in San Francisco (or current San Francisco residents for California felony Certificates of Rehabilitation).

CA.name: Stanford Law School - Community Law Clinic & Project Clean Slate
CA.what_they_offer: Law students analyze RAP sheets and assist clients with expungements, felony reductions, and early termination of probation, and also partner with San Jose State University's Record Clearance Project for record screenings.

CA.name: Fresno County Public Defender - Clean Slate Program
CA.what_they_offer: Provides reentry legal assistance for petitions to dismiss/expungement, felony reductions, Proposition 47, and Proposition 64 petitions.
CA.who_qualifies: Individuals with a Fresno County conviction or probation completed in Fresno County who are not on active probation or parole anywhere and have no open or pending criminal cases.
CA.cost: Free legal services (Live Scan fingerprinting costs $25-$40; fee waiver form available)

CA.name: San Jose State University - Record Clearance Project (RCP)
CA.area_served: Santa Clara County (court representation) and California (record reviews)
CA.what_they_offer: Undergraduate legal clinic students working under attorney supervision conduct legal rights presentations, review criminal records to advise on clearing California convictions, and provide court representation in Santa Clara County.
CA.who_qualifies: People seeking to clear California convictions, with court representation for cases in Santa Clara County.

CA.name: California Courts Self-Help Guide
CA.what_they_offer: Official court self-help portal connecting users to record-cleaning legal services, county public defender resources, form-filling instructions, and post-conviction guides for non-citizens.

CA.name: Yolo County Public Defender's Office - Record Mitigation and Community Reintegration Clinic
CA.what_they_offer: Provides post-conviction legal services including expungement, felony reductions, early probation termination, certificates of rehabilitation, record sealing, and sex-offender registry removal.
CA.who_qualifies: Eligible clients who submit a completed application packet along with a current RAP sheet, personal declaration, and character reference letters.

CA.name: Ventura County Public Defender's Office - Fresh Start Program
CA.what_they_offer: Helps clear criminal records through misdemeanor and felony expungements, record sealing, return of property, sex offender registration relief, certificates of rehabilitation, and early probation termination.
CA.who_qualifies: Eligible clients who completed probation, followed sentence terms, have no pending cases, and have generally paid off outstanding case balances.

CA.name: Marin County Public Defender - Clean Slate Services
CA.what_they_offer: Helps individuals apply to expunge eligible convictions, reduce felonies to misdemeanors, or vacate arrests or convictions.
CA.who_qualifies: People convicted of an eligible felony or misdemeanor who completed probation (or waited 1 year if no misdemeanor probation, or 2 years after prison release) and have no current sentence, supervision, or new charges.

CA.name: Alameda County Public Defenders Clean Slate Program
CA.what_they_offer: Provides free legal assistance for clean slate and criminal record clearing through walk-in clinic intakes and telephone intake.

CA.name: Bay Area Legal Aid – Reentry Legal Services
CA.what_they_offer: Provides free reentry and clean slate legal services through its legal advice line and intake at community events.

CA.name: Dads Evoking Change
CA.what_they_offer: Hosts a monthly drop-in legal clinic on the last Tuesday of the month offering consultations with civil law attorneys on Clean Slate and criminal record expungement.

AR.name: Legal Aid of Arkansas
AR.what_they_offer: Provides free civil legal help for expungements and criminal record sealing through phone advice, document preparation, legal representation, and community record-sealing clinics.
AR.who_qualifies: Low-income Arkansans whose household income is typically at or below 125% of the federal poverty guideline, though some cases allow higher income limits.

AR.name: AR Free Legal Answers
AR.what_they_offer: An online service where volunteer pro bono attorneys answer posted questions about sealing old criminal records. Attorneys provide written answers only and do not represent users in court.
AR.who_qualifies: People with low or moderate income who cannot afford a lawyer and have finished their sentence and paid all fines and fees.

AR.name: Arkansas Law Help
AR.what_they_offer: An online self-help portal created by Arkansas's legal aid providers with guides, eligibility rules, and felony and misdemeanor flowcharts for filing a Petition to Seal.

FL.name: The Legal Aid Society of the Orange County Bar Association, Inc.
FL.what_they_offer: Provides civil legal assistance and hosts pro bono clinics to help residents complete paperwork for sealing and expunging criminal records.
FL.who_qualifies: Indigent Orange County residents who meet financial and case guidelines.

FL.name: Office of Broward State Attorney Harold F. Pryor
FL.what_they_offer: Provides eligibility guidance, application assistance by phone, and periodic one-stop community workshops for arrest record sealing and expungement.
FL.who_qualifies: Adults and juveniles with a Broward County criminal charge that did not result in a conviction or had adjudication withheld.

FL.name: Florida Justice Center
FL.what_they_offer: Researches eligibility, files paperwork, and represents clients in court for criminal record sealing and expungement, along with clemency and mugshot removal.
FL.who_qualifies: Low-income people in Florida affected by involvement in the criminal legal system.

FL.name: Jacksonville Area Legal Aid, Inc.
FL.what_they_offer: Offers an online eligibility tool and legal assistance for sealing and expunging Florida criminal arrest records.
FL.who_qualifies: Residents in their service area whose Florida arrest record may be eligible to be sealed or expunged.

FL.name: Bay Area Legal Services
FL.what_they_offer: Provides legal information and civil legal help for criminal record expungement and sealing following an eligibility review.
FL.who_qualifies: Individuals in Florida who meet the organization's eligibility requirements.

FL.name: Free Legal Aid in Seminole County
FL.what_they_offer: Hosts a monthly walk-in clinic on the first Wednesday of every month where volunteer attorneys give advice on sealing and expungement.
FL.who_qualifies: Open to the public at walk-in clinics; ongoing representation requires Seminole County residency, income eligibility, and not already having an attorney.

FL.name: Public Defender's Office – Redemption Project
FL.what_they_offer: Operates a Redemption Hotline and community workshops where volunteers help people determine eligibility and apply to seal or expunge criminal records.
FL.who_qualifies: Individuals with prior arrests who qualify for sealing or expungement under Florida law.

FL.name: Community Law Program
FL.what_they_offer: Helps residents check eligibility and pursue criminal record sealing or expungement, voting rights restoration, and driver's license reinstatement.
FL.who_qualifies: Pinellas County residents experiencing barriers to employment, housing, or other needs due to criminal histories.

FL.name: Office of the Public Defender
FL.what_they_offer: Provides assistance with sealing or expunction of criminal charges, civil rights restoration, and early termination of probation.
FL.who_qualifies: Former clients represented by this Public Defender's Office who were charged with a crime without being convicted and meet eligibility rules.
FL.cost: No professional cost; approximately $130 in mandatory fees to other entities

LA.name: Justice and Accountability Center of Louisiana (JAC)
LA.area_served: New Orleans, Orleans Parish, and Jefferson Parish
LA.what_they_offer: Hosts regular walk-in expungement clinics, offers 25-minute video consultations with volunteer attorneys to complete expungement forms, provides an online fee-waiver affidavit tool, and helps applicants request income-based filing fee waivers.
LA.who_qualifies: Individuals with criminal records seeking expungement; low-income individuals may qualify for fee waivers.

LA.name: Southeast Louisiana Legal Services (SLLS)
LA.what_they_offer: Hosts free expungement clinics, operates local outreach clinics, covers background check costs at clinic events, and opens cases to file expungements for eligible clients.
LA.who_qualifies: Individuals who qualify for free legal services and have eligible offenses (certain clinics are limited to HANO public housing or voucher residents).

LA.name: Acadiana Legal Service Corporation (ALSC)
LA.area_served: St. Landry Parish, Lafayette, and rural Louisiana communities
LA.what_they_offer: Hosts free expungement clinics with pro bono attorneys and runs a Workforce Enhancement Program that helps cover background checks, court filing fees, and related expungement costs.
LA.who_qualifies: Eligible low-income residents with qualifying criminal records.

LA.name: Orleans Public Defenders
LA.what_they_offer: Partners with local legal organizations to host monthly expungement clinics where attorneys and client advocates help gather case information and fill out expungement applications.

LA.name: Louisiana Justice Coalition (LJC)
LA.what_they_offer: Collaborates with Orleans Public Defenders through the Client Expungement Initiative to engage public defenders and volunteer attorneys for expungement filings and manages a fund to help pay non-waivable filing fees.
LA.who_qualifies: Select ex-offender clients in New Orleans facing financial barriers to filing fees.
LA.cost: Financial assistance available for select clients to cover non-waivable fees

LA.name: Justice Reform Initiative (JRI)
LA.what_they_offer: Approved pro bono legal provider that hosts expungement clinics with volunteer attorneys to give expungement support and prepare documents.

LA.name: Loyola Law Clinic: Stuart H. Smith Law Clinic & Center for Social Justice
LA.what_they_offer: Law school clinic listed by the Municipal and Traffic Court of New Orleans as a legal aid resource for expungement guidance and legal assistance.
LA.who_qualifies: Indigent New Orleans residents who meet federal poverty guidelines after an intake interview and have a case type the clinic handles.

LA.name: Tulane Law Clinic: Criminal Justice Clinic
LA.what_they_offer: Law school clinic listed by the Municipal and Traffic Court of New Orleans as a legal assistance resource for expungement matters.

LA.name: Tulane Legal Assistance Program (TULAP)
LA.what_they_offer: Provides legal information and representation for criminal matters including expungements.
LA.who_qualifies: Current Tulane University students, faculty, and staff with a Tulane email address.
LA.cost: Free legal information and low-cost representation

IL.name: Cabrini Green Legal Aid
IL.what_they_offer: Provides help with expungement, record sealing, clemency, pardons, certificates of rehabilitation, and waivers. Also operates courthouse expungement help desks in Cook County and represents self-represented petitioners at hearings.
IL.who_qualifies: Individuals seeking criminal record relief in Illinois; those arrested by the Chicago Police Department must bring a Chicago RAP sheet for help desk assistance.

IL.name: James B. Moran Center for Youth Advocacy
IL.what_they_offer: Provides legal assistance to expunge or seal criminal histories and operates a weekly walk-in expungement and sealing help desk at the Skokie Courthouse.
IL.who_qualifies: All individuals with a Cook County criminal record.
IL.cost: Free legal services; court filing and record fees may apply unless waived

IL.name: Legal Aid Chicago
IL.what_they_offer: Provides full year-round representation in adult expungement, sealing, trafficking vacatur, and Aguilar motions, as well as a walk-in Juvenile Expungement Help Desk at the Cook County Juvenile Center.
IL.who_qualifies: People living in poverty who pass eligibility screening and have an eligible Cook County adult or juvenile record.

IL.name: Prairie State Legal Services
IL.what_they_offer: Hosts criminal records relief clinics where attorneys consult on record-clearing options and prepare documents to expunge or seal eligible records.
IL.who_qualifies: Low-income residents who meet financial guidelines and do not have pending criminal charges.

IL.name: Social Change
IL.what_they_offer: Runs expungement and record sealing clinics in partnership with legal advocates, providing legal representation, support through the petition process, and groceries for participating households.

IL.name: Law Office of the Cook County Public Defender
IL.what_they_offer: Holds expungement and sealing workshops alongside CARPLS and New Leaf to check record-clearing eligibility, assist with completing forms, and explain the legal process.

IL.name: Children and Family Justice Center, Northwestern Pritzker School of Law
IL.what_they_offer: Attorneys and law students help locate qualifying juvenile records, complete court paperwork, prepare clients for hearings, and attend court hearings for juvenile expungement and sealing.
IL.who_qualifies: Young people seeking to seal or expunge juvenile records under Illinois law.

IL.name: DePaul University College of Law Criminal Records Field Clinic
IL.what_they_offer: Law students working under attorney supervision through the Greater Chicago Legal Clinic analyze criminal records, draft petitions, and represent clients seeking expungement, sealing, and other record relief.

IL.name: Illinois Legal Aid Online
IL.what_they_offer: Provides online step-by-step guides, eligibility worksheets, Clean Slate Act information, and automated Easy Form tools to prepare adult, juvenile, and cannabis expungement or sealing petitions.

MA.name: Legal Services Center of Harvard Law School — Safety Net Project
MA.what_they_offer: Provides record-sealing forms, one-on-one consultations, community workshops, and legal representation for sealing and expunging Massachusetts criminal records, as well as self-help resources.
MA.who_qualifies: People who meet Massachusetts statutory eligibility criteria for criminal record sealing or expungement.
MA.cost: Free legal help ($25 fee to access CORI, waived for public benefit recipients)

MA.name: Community Legal Aid — CORI / Re-Entry Unit
MA.what_they_offer: Provides legal representation in CORI sealing and expungement cases as well as assistance with housing, employment, and training denials caused by a criminal record.

MA.name: City of Boston — Project Opportunity (Black Male Advancement)
MA.what_they_offer: Connects residents with volunteer lawyers through Lawyers Clearinghouse for virtual CORI consultations and full representation on sealing or expungement petitions and hearings.
MA.cost: Free (also covers the cost to access CORI)

MA.name: Harvard Defenders
MA.what_they_offer: Provides legal assistance to individuals seeking to seal their Massachusetts criminal records.
MA.who_qualifies: Individuals in Massachusetts who wish to seal their Massachusetts CORI.

MA.name: Center for Social Justice — Western New England University School of Law
MA.what_they_offer: Works with law students and pro bono volunteers to help clients obtain CORI reports, receive one-on-one attorney consultations, and prepare and file petitions to seal or expunge records.
MA.who_qualifies: Community members who are eligible to seal or expunge their Massachusetts CORI.

MA.name: Northeast Legal Aid
MA.area_served: Northeastern Massachusetts (Lawrence, Lynn, Lowell, and Haverhill)
MA.what_they_offer: Helps clients obtain and understand their criminal records, correct errors, and pursue sealing and expungement options through the mail or in court.
MA.who_qualifies: Low-income or elderly residents in Northeastern Massachusetts.

MO.name: Legal Services of Southern Missouri
MO.area_served: Cape Girardeau, Rolla, Sikeston, Springfield, and West Plains
MO.what_they_offer: Helps individuals expunge or close Missouri arrest, charge, and conviction records, and partners on Clean Slate Clinics offering legal representation.
MO.who_qualifies: People with eligible Missouri arrests, charges, or nonviolent low-level convictions (federal offenses do not qualify).

MO.name: Legal Services of Eastern Missouri (Volunteer Lawyers Program)
MO.what_they_offer: Provides pro bono legal representation and advice clinics through volunteer attorneys to help expunge old, non-violent criminal records.
MO.who_qualifies: Low-income individuals with old, non-violent criminal records who cannot afford an attorney.

MO.name: Mid-Missouri Legal Services
MO.what_they_offer: Provides legal assistance for the expungement of eligible criminal records through offices in Columbia and Jefferson City.

MO.name: ArchCity Defenders
MO.what_they_offer: Helps people remove past arrests and convictions through its RESTART Expungement Program alongside wraparound social services, and publishes a self-help expungement guide.

MO.name: Springfield Metropolitan Bar Association & Foundation
MO.what_they_offer: Partners with Legal Services of Southern Missouri to host Clean Slate Expungement Clinics explaining Missouri expungement law and allowing attendees to sign up for representation.
MO.who_qualifies: People previously convicted of eligible nonviolent, low-level state offenses in Missouri.

MO.name: Clear My Record Missouri
MO.what_they_offer: Provides a step-by-step 2025 Pro Se Guide, downloadable court forms packet, offense eligibility lookup list, and instructional videos for filing expungements without a lawyer (its former UMKC clinic is closed).
MO.who_qualifies: Individuals with eligible Missouri criminal records who cannot afford an attorney and do not qualify for legal aid.

MO.name: Missouri State Public Defender
MO.what_they_offer: Provides a pro se petition form to request expungement of eligible marijuana offenses, legal advice for qualifying incarcerated former clients, and a directory of Missouri expungement resources.
MO.who_qualifies: The pro se petition is for currently incarcerated people with eligible marijuana offenses; legal advice is limited to indigent people currently incarcerated on eligible marijuana offenses whom MSPD previously represented.

TX.name: Legal Aid of NorthWest Texas - Statewide Expunction Project
TX.what_they_offer: Helps clear eligible criminal records through expunctions and nondisclosure orders via direct representation, recurring virtual clinics, and library outreach events.
TX.who_qualifies: Financially eligible residents within their North Texas and Panhandle service area (income at or below 200% of the federal poverty guidelines).

TX.name: ClearPath Texas
TX.what_they_offer: Coordinates free in-person, remote, and live-chat expunction and nondisclosure clinics connecting residents with legal aid attorneys across Texas.
TX.who_qualifies: Income-eligible Texans whose cases were dismissed, resulted in acquittal, or completed deferred adjudication for certain offenses.

TX.name: Texas State Law Library
TX.what_they_offer: Provides self-help legal guides explaining Texas expunction, adult nondisclosure, and juvenile record sealing laws along with links to common court forms.

TX.name: Lone Star Legal Aid - Civil Matters in Criminal Justice Project
TX.what_they_offer: Provides civil legal representation to file applications for expungements and nondisclosure orders, repair inaccurate background checks, and access criminal records.
TX.who_qualifies: Residents in their East Texas and Houston service area whose income is at or below 125% of the Federal Poverty Line.

TX.name: University of Texas School of Law - Expunction Project
TX.what_they_offer: Pro bono law school program with intakes in September and February that helps determine eligibility and prepare court paperwork to expunge or seal criminal records.
TX.who_qualifies: People who cannot afford to hire an attorney.

TX.name: Texas Fair Defense Project
TX.what_they_offer: Provides legal assistance to seal or destroy eligible Texas criminal records through nondisclosures and expunctions; note that intake is currently closed to new applicants.
TX.who_qualifies: Applicants entitled to record clearing under Texas law whose income is within 200% of the federal poverty guidelines and who submit a DPS Criminal History Report.

TX.name: Justice Reform Foundation - Expungement Program
TX.what_they_offer: Screens criminal records, prepares expunction or nondisclosure petitions with supervised law students, and files petitions with the court.
TX.who_qualifies: Texans with qualifying dismissed charges, acquittals, uncharged arrests, certain Class C misdemeanors, or completed deferred adjudications who could not otherwise afford legal help.

TX.name: University of Houston Law Center - Records Sealing and Expunction Clinic
TX.what_they_offer: Law school clinic where students assist clients with juvenile records sealing, adult criminal record expunctions, and adult nondisclosure orders.

TX.name: Texas A&M University School of Law - Criminal Defense Clinic
TX.area_served: Tarrant County and statewide via JRF Expungement Program
TX.what_they_offer: Student interns screen records and prepare expunction and nondisclosure petitions in partnership with the Justice Reform Foundation.
TX.who_qualifies: Eligible Texans who cannot afford legal representation.

TX.name: Texas Legal Services Center
TX.what_they_offer: Provides free legal assistance to help Texans seal or expunge eligible criminal records.
TX.who_qualifies: Generally requires applicants to meet income guidelines.

TX.name: Texas RioGrande Legal Aid
TX.area_served: Central & West Texas, Rio Grande Valley
TX.what_they_offer: Legal aid organization providing free legal assistance with criminal record sealing and expunctions.
TX.who_qualifies: Income-eligible residents living within their Central Texas, West Texas, and Rio Grande Valley service area.

TX.name: Travis County Law Library
TX.what_they_offer: Listed resource offering free assistance with criminal record sealing and expunctions.

TX.name: Volunteer Legal Services of Central Texas
TX.what_they_offer: Offers free legal assistance with record sealing and expunctions, including monthly in-person legal advice clinics by appointment.
TX.who_qualifies: Residents of Travis, Hays, Bastrop, and Williamson counties who meet income eligibility requirements.

TX.name: Jefferson County Bar Association Pro Bono Program
TX.what_they_offer: Provides pro bono legal assistance for criminal record sealing and expunctions in Southeast Texas.
TX.who_qualifies: Qualifying residents of Jefferson, Hardin, and Orange counties.

TX.name: Dallas Volunteer Attorney Program
TX.what_they_offer: Provides free legal help and ongoing in-person legal clinics for criminal record sealing and expunctions.
TX.who_qualifies: Residents in the Dallas area meeting program income and service area requirements.

TX.name: Unlocking Doors
TX.area_served: Dallas, Collin, Denton, Kaufman, Rockwall, Tarrant, and Ellis counties
TX.what_they_offer: Assists individuals in the Dallas and Fort Worth areas (in partnership with Cornerstone Assistance Center in Fort Worth) with record sealing and expunction services.
TX.who_qualifies: Qualifying residents of Dallas, Collin, Denton, Kaufman, Rockwall, Tarrant, and Ellis counties.

MT.name: Montana Legal Services Association (MLSA)
MT.what_they_offer: Offers free legal help, Clean Slate clinics, representation for domestic violence survivors seeking record relief, and step-by-step texting guidance via What's Next Text (text START to 406-430-8585). Also publishes free self-help forms and instructions on MontanaLawHelp.org for misdemeanor expungement and dismissing deferred sentences.
MT.who_qualifies: Low-income Montanans with Montana misdemeanor convictions, with dedicated representation resources for survivors of domestic violence.

MT.name: Montana Judicial Branch
MT.what_they_offer: Provides official self-help packets with forms and step-by-step instructions for expunging Montana misdemeanor convictions, along with resources and forms for expunging marijuana-related convictions.
MT.who_qualifies: People seeking to expunge eligible Montana state court misdemeanor or marijuana-related convictions, excluding non-marijuana felonies and out-of-state or Tribal convictions.

KS.name: Kansas Legal Services
KS.what_they_offer: Offers free legal assistance, an online guided interview, and in-person and virtual clinics across Kansas to help expunge arrest records, criminal convictions, juvenile adjudications, and drug registry requirements.
KS.who_qualifies: Vulnerable Kansans who meet legal and program eligibility criteria determined by Kansas Legal Services.

KS.name: University of Kansas School of Law Legal Aid Clinic
KS.what_they_offer: Law student interns supervised by attorneys provide legal representation for criminal record expungements in Douglas County District Court and Lawrence Municipal Court, and host Clean Slate expungement clinics.
KS.who_qualifies: Low-income individuals with household income up to 250% of the federal poverty level, subject to clinic capacity and conflict screening.
KS.cost: Free legal representation; clients pay court filing fees unless waived

KS.name: Leavenworth County Attorney's Office Expungement Day
KS.what_they_offer: Annual program where the County Attorney's office reviews submitted expungement forms for eligibility and pairs applicants with volunteer local attorneys to answer questions and explain the process.
KS.who_qualifies: Individuals with eligible adult convictions, arrests, or diversions in Leavenworth County, excluding federal and municipal court cases.
KS.cost: Free legal services; court filing fees and surcharges apply unless waived

KS.name: Kansas Judicial Branch Self-Help
KS.what_they_offer: Official state court self-help portal providing adult expungement forms, instructions, links to free guided interviews, and directions for finding criminal history records.
KS.cost: Free online resources and guided interviews

KS.name: KC Digital Drive - Kansas Expungement Assistance
KS.what_they_offer: Provides an online self-help tool across all 105 Kansas counties that checks expungement and fee-assistance eligibility and automatically generates completed expungement petition forms for filing.
KS.who_qualifies: Self-help applicants and pro bono or staff attorneys handling Kansas expungement cases.
KS.cost: Free online tool; court filing fees apply unless waived

NM.name: New Mexico Legal Aid
NM.what_they_offer: Provides free civil legal assistance, pro se expungement form packets, limited-scope help through its Volunteer Attorney Program, and expungement representation for qualifying veterans.
NM.who_qualifies: Low-income New Mexicans and veterans who meet case criteria; Volunteer Attorney Program applicants must have household income at or below 200% of the Federal Poverty Level and meet asset limits.

NM.name: New Mexico Courts
NM.what_they_offer: Provides an online application to expunge cannabis-related court records, online case lookup tools, and downloadable forms and instructions for petitioning district courts to expunge other arrest and conviction records.
NM.who_qualifies: People with qualifying New Mexico records involving cannabis, identity theft, charges released without conviction, or eligible convictions after completing sentences and waiting periods.

NM.name: Silver City Gospel Mission
NM.what_they_offer: Offers a local step-by-step expungement resource guide and staff support to walk individuals through gathering court case records and connecting with legal aid.

WV.name: Legal Aid of West Virginia
WV.what_they_offer: Provides free civil legal help, online legal information, and community clinics to assist with expunging or sealing eligible criminal records. They also work with substance use recovery programs and Jobs & Hope WV to clear criminal records and reinstate driver's licenses.
WV.who_qualifies: Generally serves low-income individuals or victims of domestic violence, with exceptions including referrals from partnered substance use recovery programs.
WV.cost: Free (some court filing fees may be required)

WV.name: Jobs & Hope West Virginia
WV.what_they_offer: Employs transition agents across the state to help participants overcome barriers to employment and connects them with Legal Aid of West Virginia for criminal record expungement and free clinics.
WV.who_qualifies: Open to all West Virginians seeking to overcome employment barriers, whether in substance use recovery or not.

WV.name: WV Public Defender Services
WV.what_they_offer: Provides an online legal aid resource directory with access to West Virginia court expungement forms and referrals to civil legal services.

ME.name: Pine Tree Legal Assistance
ME.what_they_offer: Provides statewide civil legal aid to low-income Mainers, including help with criminal record sealing and reentry legal matters.
ME.who_qualifies: Low-income Mainers, generally with household income at or below 125% of the federal poverty level.

ME.name: State of Maine Judicial Branch
ME.what_they_offer: Publishes official self-help instructions on criminal record sealing eligibility and provides the court form (Motion to Seal Criminal History, CR-218) for filing without a lawyer.
ME.who_qualifies: People with eligible criminal convictions in Maine who meet statutory waiting period and conviction-free requirements.

UT.name: Clean Slate Utah
UT.what_they_offer: Offers free record screenings, weekly fingerprinting clinics with USARA, expungement application support, pardon support, referrals to legal resources, and financial help with government fees.
UT.who_qualifies: Individuals representing themselves; those with incomes at or below 225% of the federal poverty line may qualify for help covering the $65 application fee.

UT.name: Pro Bono Initiative — S.J. Quinney College of Law
UT.what_they_offer: Hosts a free monthly expungement clinic on the first Thursday of the month offering brief legal consultations on expungements, outstanding warrants, and misdemeanor procedural issues.
UT.who_qualifies: Members of the Utah community who call Utah Legal Services first to determine if they qualify for an expungement.

UT.name: Utah Legal Services
UT.what_they_offer: Provides free legal assistance across Utah, with state and community directories listing help for criminal record expungements and ULS also assisting with eviction expungements.
UT.who_qualifies: Individuals who apply and qualify for services, though ULS's website notes it can only provide legal help in non-criminal cases.

UT.name: Cottages of Hope
UT.what_they_offer: Provides expungement assistance alongside employment coaching to help individuals with criminal records move forward.
UT.who_qualifies: People with a criminal background, including individuals with felony convictions.

UT.name: ALIGHT (Alliance to Lead Impact in Global Human Trafficking)
UT.what_they_offer: Connects human trafficking survivors with local volunteer lawyers who offer free legal help and representation for criminal records and other legal issues.
UT.who_qualifies: Survivors of sex or labor human trafficking who cannot afford legal help and are in a place where they can focus on their legal case.

UT.name: Salt Lake County Office of Homelessness & Criminal Justice Reform
UT.what_they_offer: Provides an online self-help Expungement Tool Kit with step-by-step guides and forms for petition-based expungements, traffic expungements, 402 conviction reductions, and court fee waivers.

UT.name: Utah State Courts
UT.what_they_offer: Offers official court self-help instructions and eligibility tools for adult criminal record expungement, automatic Clean Slate expungement, and online case status checks.

UT.name: Utah Bureau of Criminal Identification (BCI)
UT.what_they_offer: Processes automatic Clean Slate expungements with the Utah courts and provides expungement forms and official letters verifying expunged criminal history.
UT.who_qualifies: Individuals with qualifying acquittals, dismissals with prejudice, or eligible misdemeanor and infraction convictions after required waiting periods.
UT.cost: Free for automatic expungement; $15 fee to request a letter listing expunged records

NC.name: Legal Aid of North Carolina
NC.what_they_offer: Holds free online expunction clinics, provides self-help materials, and offers direct legal representation for expunctions through its Second Chance Project (including Second Chance Wilmington).
NC.who_qualifies: Clinics are open to everyone with no restrictions; direct representation is for eligible low-income residents who apply during the first full week of the month (except June and December).

NC.name: Durham Expunction & Restoration Program (DEAR)
NC.what_they_offer: Provides legal help to expunge criminal charges and convictions, obtain Certificates of Relief, and restore suspended driver's licenses, along with monthly education workshops and intake.
NC.who_qualifies: Durham County residents who cannot afford an attorney and meet state eligibility criteria for expungements or Certificates of Relief.

NC.name: The Blanchard Community Law Clinic (Campbell Law School)
NC.what_they_offer: Provides pro bono criminal record expunction assistance in partnership with Triangle-area community nonprofits.
NC.who_qualifies: Low-income individuals with prior involvement in the criminal justice system.

NC.name: Emancipate NC
NC.what_they_offer: Hosts a pro bono criminal record expungement clinic connecting community members with legal assistance and information on record relief.
NC.who_qualifies: Eligible community members seeking relief from barriers caused by a criminal record.

NC.name: Carolina Student Legal Services, Inc. (CSLS)
NC.what_they_offer: Provides legal representation for most North Carolina criminal record expunctions and legal advice for traffic and criminal matters.
NC.who_qualifies: UNC students, provided the matter is not against another UNC student, the University, or the state of North Carolina.

NC.name: NC Second Chance Alliance
NC.what_they_offer: Publishes self-help guides, FAQs on North Carolina's Second Chance Act, and links to expungement petition and fee waiver forms.

NH.name: 603 Legal Aid
NH.what_they_offer: Provides free civil legal representation, advocacy, volunteer attorney referrals, and online self-help guides for annulling arrest records and non-violent convictions.
NH.who_qualifies: Eligible low-income and economically disadvantaged people in New Hampshire.

NH.name: New Hampshire Legal Assistance
NH.what_they_offer: Provides civil legal aid and reentry legal assistance to help clear criminal records through annulment and address reentry barriers. Intake applications are handled online or by phone through 603 Legal Aid.
NH.who_qualifies: Low-income New Hampshire residents with limited assets (generally at or below 125% of the federal poverty level) and older adults age 60 and over.

NH.name: New Hampshire Law Library
NH.what_they_offer: Maintains an online legal help guide for criminal record annulments and offers public computers, research materials, and staff guidance on how to use legal research tools.
NH.who_qualifies: Open to anyone in the public.

NH.name: New Hampshire Bar Association
NH.what_they_offer: Runs LawLine, a monthly phone clinic on the second Wednesday from 6 to 8 PM where volunteer lawyers answer general legal questions, as well as the Modest Means Legal Program connecting callers to reduced-rate lawyers.
NH.who_qualifies: LawLine is open to the public at all income levels; Modest Means serves qualified lower- and middle-income individuals who do not qualify for free civil legal aid.
NH.cost: Free for LawLine; reduced rates for Modest Means Legal Program

NH.name: New Hampshire Free Legal Answers
NH.what_they_offer: Operates a confidential virtual legal advice clinic where users post civil legal questions online and receive emailed answers from a volunteer New Hampshire attorney.
NH.who_qualifies: Qualifying users with civil legal questions.

CO.name: Expunge Colorado
CO.what_they_offer: Runs an annual record sealing clinic and provides pro bono petition-based record sealing services, educational guides, and community support.

CO.name: Northwest Colorado Legal Services Project
CO.area_served: Clear Creek, Delta, Eagle, Grand, Gunnison, Hinsdale, Lake, Moffat, Montrose, Ouray, Routt, San Miguel, and Summit counties
CO.what_they_offer: Provides an ongoing record sealing and expungement clinic where an attorney reviews Colorado criminal records for eligibility and helps complete court forms.
CO.who_qualifies: Low-income clients with criminal records in the served counties.

CO.name: Transformative Justice Project of Colorado
CO.what_they_offer: Offers legal representation, record expungement support, and reintegration assistance through its Believe in Youth program (formerly Colorado Juvenile Defender Center).
CO.who_qualifies: System-impacted young people ages 10 to 25 and individuals with juvenile records.

CO.name: Colorado Legal Services
CO.area_served: Adams, Alamosa, Arapahoe, Archuleta, Boulder, Broomfield, Chaffee, Conejos, Costilla, Custer, Denver, Dolores, Douglas, El Paso, Elbert, Fremont, Hinsdale, Jefferson, La Plata, Lincoln, Mineral, Montezuma, Ouray, Park, Rio Grande, Saguache, San Juan, San Miguel, and Teller counties; seniors in Clear Creek and Gilpin counties; Ute Mountain Ute and Southern Ute reservations
CO.what_they_offer: Provides civil legal aid including record clearance assistance through offices in Alamosa, Boulder, Colorado Springs, Denver, and Durango.

CO.name: Colorado Criminal Defense Institute
CO.what_they_offer: Listed as a statewide organization engaging in criminal record clearance work in Colorado.

CO.name: El Paso County Bar Association
CO.what_they_offer: Local bar association listed as engaging in criminal record clearance work.

CO.name: Colorado Clean Slate Coalition
CO.what_they_offer: Provides an online tool to estimate eligibility for automated record sealing in Colorado and educational resources on Clean Slate and petition-based sealing.

SC.name: LifeWorks SC
SC.what_they_offer: Provides application support, forms, guidance from attorneys and volunteers, and free Thursday clinics for South Carolina expungements and pardons through its Second Chance Program. Also offers funds to help offset or cover filing fees when available.
SC.who_qualifies: Individuals submitting expungement or pardon applications for offenses committed in South Carolina, with fee help for those needing financial assistance.
SC.cost: Free clinics and support; financial assistance for fees when available

SC.name: Charleston Pro Bono Legal Services
SC.what_they_offer: Helps residents check expungement eligibility, understand their legal options, and prepare and file expungement petitions to clear eligible criminal records.
SC.who_qualifies: Charleston County residents with a household income at or below 80% of the Area Median Income.

SC.name: South Carolina Legal Services
SC.what_they_offer: Provides free civil legal services, educational brochures, brief-service clinics, and representation to help residents obtain South Carolina expungements and pardons.
SC.who_qualifies: Financially eligible applicants, typically with household incomes at or below 125% of the federal poverty level (or up to 200% with a waiver), seeking expungements to access employment, housing, or public benefits.

SC.name: Time Served
SC.what_they_offer: Offers free legal advocacy and assistance with record expungements and pardons to help formerly incarcerated people rebuild stability.
SC.who_qualifies: Currently and formerly incarcerated individuals in South Carolina.

SC.name: Ministries of Hope
SC.what_they_offer: Provides virtual expungement and pardon clinic informational videos in partnership with South Carolina Legal Services and helps cover legal processing fees.
SC.who_qualifies: Eligible clinic attendees with South Carolina criminal records.
SC.cost: Pays up to 100% of legal processing fees for eligible attendees

SC.name: South Carolina Judicial Branch
SC.what_they_offer: Publishes official self-help FAQs explaining South Carolina expungement and pardon eligibility rules and how to apply for record destruction orders.
SC.cost: Free information; no court fee to expunge non-convictions

SC.name: Sixth Judicial Circuit Solicitor's Office
SC.what_they_offer: Processes expungement orders directly for applicants without requiring a private attorney, waiving fees for eligible non-convictions.
SC.who_qualifies: Individuals with eligible arrests or convictions in the Sixth Judicial Circuit.
SC.cost: Free for non-convictions; $250 administrative fee, $35 clerk fee, and $25 SLED fee for convictions

SC.name: Eleventh Judicial Circuit Solicitor's Office
SC.area_served: Edgefield, Lexington, McCormick, and Saluda Counties
SC.what_they_offer: Provides an expungement application packet to help determine eligibility and processes expungement requests through a dedicated coordinator.
SC.who_qualifies: Individuals whose eligible arrests occurred in Edgefield, Lexington, McCormick, or Saluda County.

SC.name: 15th Judicial Circuit Solicitor's Office
SC.what_they_offer: Provides downloadable expungement screening applications and processes expungement requests for qualifying local charges, though staff cannot give legal advice.
SC.who_qualifies: Individuals whose eligible charges were prosecuted in Horry or Georgetown County.

DE.name: Delaware Office of Defense Services - Post Disposition Unit
DE.what_they_offer: Reviews Delaware criminal records to check expungement and pardon eligibility, operates an expungement hotline and online screening form, and hosts free expungement clinics with attorneys. Its Appellate Division also represents youth and indigent adults in expungements and pardons.
DE.who_qualifies: Youth, indigent adults, and individuals with Delaware criminal records seeking eligibility screening.

DE.name: APEX Program - Delaware Department of Labor
