DE.what_they_offer: Provides non-attorney one-on-one guidance through the pardon and expungement application process, help gathering documents and completing paperwork, and preparation classes for Board of Pardons hearings.
DE.who_qualifies: Individuals with Delaware offenses and no pending charges who either have never been convicted of an adult offense or have not been arrested, incarcerated, or on probation or parole in the past 3 years.

DE.name: Delaware Volunteer Legal Services (DVLS)
DE.what_they_offer: Volunteer attorneys review criminal background records to determine whether an individual is eligible for an expungement or a pardon.
DE.who_qualifies: Community members who have low incomes or are victims of domestic violence.

DE.name: Clean Slate Delaware - ACLU of Delaware
DE.what_they_offer: Provides public guides and resources on Delaware's automated Clean Slate expungement process and co-hosts community expungement clinics with attorneys and pardon specialists.

DE.name: Delaware Center for Justice
DE.what_they_offer: Provides financial assistance to cover expungement fees and legal support for people reentering the community after incarceration.

DE.name: Delaware State Courts - Expungement & Pardon Help
DE.what_they_offer: Provides official self-help petition forms, instruction packets, and FAQs for filing adult and juvenile criminal record expungements in Superior Court and Family Court.

DE.name: Delaware Board of Pardons
DE.what_they_offer: Provides official eligibility information and application instructions for seeking a Delaware pardon, expungement, or commutation.

WY.name: Legal Aid of Wyoming, Inc.
WY.what_they_offer: Provides civil legal advice through a telephone hotline and extended legal representation for criminal record expungements, with a tribal advocate on staff for Wind River Indian Reservation members.
WY.who_qualifies: Low-income citizens of Wyoming who are screened and qualified.

WY.name: University of Wyoming College of Law Civil Legal Services Clinic
WY.what_they_offer: A statewide law school clinic that assists Wyoming residents with civil legal matters, including criminal record expungements.
WY.who_qualifies: Wyoming residents who meet income qualification requirements.

WY.name: Wyoming Judicial Branch
WY.what_they_offer: Official court self-help resource providing expungement forms, answers to common questions, and an overview of procedures and eligibility for sealing Wyoming criminal records.

PA.name: Philadelphia Lawyers for Social Equity (PLSE)
PA.what_they_offer: Conducts community record-clearing clinics and represents clients by reviewing, filing, and arguing expungement petitions in the Philadelphia Court of Common Pleas, as well as assisting with pardons.
PA.who_qualifies: People with household incomes below 200% of the federal poverty guidelines who have convictions in Philadelphia County (for expungements) or live in Philadelphia County (for pardons).

PA.name: Legal Aid of Southeastern Pennsylvania (LASP)
PA.area_served: Bucks, Chester, Delaware, and Montgomery counties
PA.what_they_offer: Helps clients with expungements and Clean Slate record sealing through direct assistance, virtual and in-person clinics, and county-specific self-help guides.

PA.name: MidPenn Legal Services
PA.area_served: Adams, Bedford, Berks, Blair, Centre, Clearfield, Cumberland, Dauphin, Franklin, Fulton, Huntingdon, Juniata, Lancaster, Lebanon, Mifflin, Perry, Schuylkill, and York counties
PA.what_they_offer: Assists individuals in clearing criminal records through expungements, record sealing, and pardons under its Employment Law Project, with specialized expungement help for domestic and sexual violence survivors in select counties.
PA.who_qualifies: Eligible individuals in civil cases, including survivors of domestic and sexual violence in participating counties.

PA.name: Community Forgiveness & Restoration Initiative (CFRI) – CFR Legal Clinic
PA.what_they_offer: Assists returning citizens with legal consultations, document preparation, and filing applications for expungement and criminal record sealing.

PA.name: Summit Legal Aid
PA.what_they_offer: Works with clients to check criminal records and petition for full or partial expungements and record sealing, and participates in the Pardon Project of Washington County.
PA.who_qualifies: Eligible clients; the Washington County Pardon Project serves people living in or with a nonviolent record in Washington County who have been off probation or parole for over three years.

PA.name: Montgomery County Public Defender Office
PA.what_they_offer: Holds twice-monthly Zoom expungement clinics where advocates meet one-on-one with clients to check eligibility and assist with expunging or sealing closed juvenile and adult cases.
PA.who_qualifies: Current and former clients who were represented by the Montgomery County Public Defender Office on the closed cases they want expunged or sealed, with assessed fines and fees paid.

PA.name: Philadelphia Bar Association – Young Lawyers Division Expungement Clinic
PA.what_they_offer: Volunteer attorneys help eligible individuals get prior arrests and convictions expunged or sealed from public view.
PA.who_qualifies: Individuals who meet legal eligibility requirements for expungement or sealing.

PA.name: Allegheny County Office of the Public Defender – Project Reset
PA.what_they_offer: Provides an expungement guide, answers questions by email about expungement and petition-based record sealing, and conducts targeted outreach to notify local residents of their eligibility.

PA.name: University of Pennsylvania Carey Law School – Criminal Record Expungement Project (C-REP)
PA.what_they_offer: Law school student volunteers partner with Philadelphia Lawyers for Social Equity to conduct client intake clinics, process applications, and file petitions to expunge and redact non-conviction records.

IN.name: Neighborhood Christian Legal Clinic
IN.what_they_offer: Operates an Expungement Help Desk that assists individuals with applying to clear criminal records under Indiana's Second Chance law, as well as offering periodic community screening workshops.
IN.who_qualifies: Individuals earning at or below 125% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines, with some flexibility for those slightly above.

IN.name: Indiana Legal Services
IN.what_they_offer: Provides legal advice and representation to expunge or seal criminal records in Indiana state courts, including services through its Bloomington Expungement Help Desk and Military Assistance Project.
IN.who_qualifies: People earning below 125% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines (up to 200% in some cases), including income-eligible veterans, who also meet asset and citizenship or immigration status rules.

IN.name: Indiana University Bloomington Student Legal Services
IN.what_they_offer: Licensed attorneys and legal interns provide confidential legal advice and assist eligible students with expunging criminal records.
IN.cost: Free (covered by student activity fee; court fees are not covered)

IN.name: Marion County Clerk’s Office – Juvenile Division
IN.what_they_offer: Provides expungement applications and procedural information for individuals seeking a court ruling to expunge juvenile court records.

IN.name: Indiana Legal Help
IN.what_they_offer: Provides online self-help information explaining Indiana criminal expungement eligibility rules, where to file petitions, and how to find local legal services programs.

NJ.name: New Jersey Office of the Public Defender (NJOPD) Expungement Unit
NJ.what_they_offer: Hosts free community expungement clinics where attorneys screen individuals for eligibility, help prepare expungement applications, and go to court on their behalf. They also offer workshops on pardons and clemency.
NJ.who_qualifies: Eligible New Jersey residents seeking to clear their criminal records.

NJ.name: Volunteer Lawyers for Justice (VLJ) - ReLeSe Program
NJ.what_they_offer: Runs virtual monthly legal clinics to check expungement eligibility and help clients e-file pro se petitions. Complex cases are placed with pro bono attorneys for full representation, and volunteers also help answer objections.
NJ.who_qualifies: Individuals with New Jersey criminal records who pass financial screening.

NJ.name: Rutgers Law School Expungement Law Project
NJ.what_they_offer: Supervised law students provide pro bono legal representation to help clear New Jersey criminal records, as well as community information sessions and consultation clinics.
NJ.who_qualifies: Low-income individuals seeking expungement of their New Jersey criminal history.

NJ.name: NNJLS
NJ.what_they_offer: Reviews criminal records to advise on expungement eligibility and files petitions with the court to seal dismissed cases, eligible convictions, or clean sweep conviction groups.

NJ.name: South Jersey Legal Services, Inc. (SJLS) - The Expungement Project
NJ.what_they_offer: Staff and volunteer attorneys help clients obtain expungements of their New Jersey criminal records, excluding out-of-state and involuntary civil commitment records.
NJ.who_qualifies: Income-eligible individuals whose New Jersey expungement cases meet the organization's board guidelines.

NJ.name: Legal Services of New Jersey (LSNJ) - Reentry Project
NJ.what_they_offer: Provides civil legal assistance, individual representation, and educational guides for expungements, pardon applications, and correcting errors on criminal records and background checks.
NJ.who_qualifies: People with limited income in New Jersey.

NJ.name: New Jersey Courts (eCourts Expungement System)
NJ.what_they_offer: Provides a free online system to file expungement petitions, along with case number lookup tools, step-by-step user guides, instructional videos, and local court ombudsman support.

HI.name: Hawaiʻi Criminal Justice Data Center (Department of the Attorney General)
HI.what_they_offer: State agency that processes applications to expunge non-conviction arrest records and qualifying conviction records. For orders granted on or after July 1, 2025, it automatically sends the expungement order to the Judiciary to seal or remove related court case records.
HI.who_qualifies: People arrested or charged with a crime in Hawaii without a resulting conviction (subject to statutory exclusions and waiting periods), or individuals with court orders for certain first-time drug or under-21 alcohol driving convictions.
HI.cost: $35 for a first-time expungement; $50 for a subsequent expungement

HI.name: Beyond Guilt Hawaiʻi – William S. Richardson School of Law
HI.what_they_offer: Law school clinic started with the Hawaiʻi Innocence Project that offers free legal help with expungements, court case sealing, pardons, commutations, compassionate release, and parole. Law school students and staff also assist volunteer attorneys at free community expungement clinics.
HI.who_qualifies: Formerly or currently incarcerated individuals contesting unjust sentences or people seeking assistance with record clearing, clemency, drug offenses, or parole.

HI.name: Legal Aid Society of Hawaii (LASH)
HI.what_they_offer: Provides free legal assistance with criminal record expungement cases through offices on all major islands following an application, income check, and case review.
HI.who_qualifies: Low-income residents who meet income eligibility limits, typically around 125% of the federal poverty guidelines.

HI.name: Volunteer Legal Services Hawaiʻi (VLSH)
HI.what_they_offer: Coordinates volunteer pro bono attorneys to provide free legal advice and expungement assistance at periodic community clinics on Oʻahu and the neighbor islands.
HI.who_qualifies: Residents who meet income eligibility limits, typically around 125% of the federal poverty guidelines.

VT.name: Vermont Legal Aid and Legal Services Vermont
VT.what_they_offer: Provides online self-help guides on VTLawHelp.org explaining how to seal or expunge Vermont criminal records, as well as civil legal services and periodic community expungement clinics with attorneys.
VT.who_qualifies: Eligible Vermonters seeking civil legal services or attending partner clinics.

VT.name: Office of the Vermont Attorney General
VT.what_they_offer: Hosts periodic criminal record clearing clinics across Vermont where attorneys from the Attorney General's Office help prepare petitions to seal or expunge qualifying convictions and dismissed charges.
VT.who_qualifies: Members of the public with qualifying Vermont criminal convictions or dismissed charges who book an appointment in advance.

VT.name: Center for Justice Reform Clinic at Vermont Law and Graduate School
VT.what_they_offer: Law and graduate student clinicians work under attorney supervision to help individuals prepare and submit petitions to seal or expunge criminal convictions.

VT.name: South Royalton Legal Clinic at Vermont Law and Graduate School
VT.what_they_offer: Student clinicians supervised by staff attorneys represent clients in civil legal matters, including helping veterans with criminal record expungement.
VT.who_qualifies: Eligible veterans who complete the clinic's intake screening process.

VT.name: Vermont Judiciary Resource and Access Center
VT.what_they_offer: Helps people navigate the Vermont court system, fill out court forms, and handle administrative steps for criminal record expungement.

VT.name: Center for Restorative Justice
VT.what_they_offer: Offers guidance and hands-on assistance to people filing court petitions to clear their past criminal records.

VT.name: The Root Social Justice Center
VT.what_they_offer: Partners with Vermont Legal Aid to host in-person clinics in Brattleboro where an attorney helps participants expunge Vermont criminal records.
VT.who_qualifies: Black, Indigenous, and People of Color (BIPOC) Vermonters seeking help with Vermont criminal charges.

NE.name: Legal Aid of Nebraska
NE.what_they_offer: Provides free legal representation, periodic record-clearing clinics, and online step-by-step guides to help seal adult and juvenile records, set aside criminal convictions, and pursue pardons.
NE.who_qualifies: US citizens and lawful permanent residents with limited household income and assets (generally 125% of the federal poverty level, though exceptions apply for seniors 60+ and public clinics).
NE.cost: Free legal services (clients may have to pay court costs)

NE.name: University of Nebraska College of Law - Nebraska Innocence Clinic & Clean Slate Project
NE.what_they_offer: Offers pro bono legal assistance and direct representation to set aside criminal convictions, obtain pardons, and seal adult and juvenile criminal records.
NE.who_qualifies: Qualifying Nebraskans, including veterans, non-veterans, and survivors of human trafficking.

NE.name: Nebraska Judicial Branch Self-Help Center
NE.what_they_offer: Provides online self-help instructions, a Clean Slate Eligibility Questionnaire, and a guided form-completion tool for adult and juvenile record sealing, conviction set-asides, and pardons.
NE.cost: Free online tools (small fees apply if ordering criminal history records)

MD.name: Maryland Legal Aid
MD.what_they_offer: Provides free civil legal help for criminal record expungements, including eligibility reviews, same-day petition drafting at community clinics, and representation in expungement hearings through 12 offices.
MD.who_qualifies: Financially eligible low-income individuals and households (most clients have incomes at or below 125% of the federal poverty guidelines).

MD.name: Maryland Center for Legal Assistance (MCLA)
MD.area_served: Statewide (via phone, live chat, and walk-in Help Centers across Maryland)
MD.what_they_offer: Provides legal advice and education through the Maryland Courts Help Centers to help self-represented individuals handle civil matters including criminal record expungements.
MD.who_qualifies: All people, regardless of means or background.

MD.name: Community Legal Services of Prince George's County
MD.what_they_offer: Helps people complete expungement petitions through external clinic events, online intake, and legal representation.
MD.who_qualifies: All eligible Marylanders, regardless of income.

MD.name: Maryland Volunteer Lawyers Service (MVLS)
MD.what_they_offer: Provides legal assistance to individuals seeking expungement of their criminal record through online and telephone intake.
MD.who_qualifies: Individuals who meet specific income eligibility and geographical location requirements.

MD.name: Civil Justice, Inc.
MD.what_they_offer: Operates a legal referral service connecting individuals with reduced-fee (low/mid-bono) attorneys for criminal record expungement help.
MD.who_qualifies: Low to moderate income individuals who may not qualify for Maryland Legal Aid or Maryland Volunteer Lawyers Service.

MD.name: HPRP
MD.area_served: Baltimore City, Montgomery County, and Prince George's County
MD.what_they_offer: Conducts community-based, hybrid, and telephone expungement intakes to determine if individuals can petition the court to remove criminal charges from their records.
MD.who_qualifies: Homeless and low-income persons with Maryland state criminal records.

MD.name: Office of the Public Defender
MD.area_served: Statewide (including Baltimore City and Prince George's County)
MD.what_they_offer: Provides expungement, record shielding, MVA expungement, and pardon resource manuals and information, as well as the Prince George's County CARE Program.

IA.name: Iowa Legal Aid
IA.what_they_offer: Provides free legal representation and clinics across Iowa to help expunge eligible adult criminal and juvenile records, as well as help with court debt and driver's license barriers.
IA.who_qualifies: Low-income Iowans generally earning up to 125% of the federal poverty level (or up to 200% in some cases), veterans, people aged 60 or older, and survivors of domestic abuse.

IA.name: Des Moines Abolition Coalition and Des Moines Mutual Aid
IA.what_they_offer: Helps individuals expunge qualifying Iowa criminal records, such as dismissed or acquitted charges, from public view.
IA.who_qualifies: Available to anyone with qualifying Iowa criminal records.

IA.name: Iowa Judicial Branch
IA.what_they_offer: Provides self-help court forms that individuals without a lawyer can file to request expungement of eligible criminal records.
IA.who_qualifies: People without an attorney seeking to expunge eligible court records.

IA.name: Iowa State Bar Association
IA.what_they_offer: Operates Iowa Free Legal Answers for limited online pro bono legal advice and the Find-A-Lawyer directory of licensed attorneys who assist with expungements.
IA.who_qualifies: Users must complete online screening questions to qualify for Iowa Free Legal Answers; anyone can use the Find-A-Lawyer directory.
IA.cost: Free for qualifying Iowa Free Legal Answers users; $25 or less for up to 30 minutes of initial consultation through Find-A-Lawyer

IA.name: University of Iowa Student Legal Services
IA.what_they_offer: Provides legal guidance and consultations regarding Iowa criminal record expungements for university students.

AL.name: Legal Services Alabama
AL.what_they_offer: Provides free legal representation, virtual and in-person expungement clinics, and criminal record sealing or expungement assistance for veterans.
AL.who_qualifies: Low-income Alabamians with eligible charges, as well as qualifying veterans who were discharged under conditions other than dishonorable or are at risk of homelessness.

AL.name: Volunteer Lawyers Birmingham
AL.what_they_offer: Offers expungement clinics, step-by-step client guides, and legal assistance to clear eligible criminal charges and misdemeanor convictions.
AL.who_qualifies: Low-income residents of Jefferson County who have a qualifying charge or conviction.

AL.name: University of Alabama School of Law Criminal Defense Clinic
AL.area_served: Tuscaloosa and nearby areas (within 1 hour of the law school)
AL.what_they_offer: Law students under faculty supervision provide free legal help with expungements, minor offenses, eligibility screenings, and fee waiver motions.
AL.who_qualifies: People who cannot afford a lawyer with cases in a courthouse within one hour of the law school, excluding felony charges, incarcerated individuals unable to make bail, and people who already have a public defender.

AL.name: AlabamaLegalHelp.org
AL.what_they_offer: Provides an online self-help guide explaining Alabama expungement eligibility, required records, and links to the expungement petition and fee-waiver forms.
AL.cost: Free online information (filing and record fees apply unless waived via Affidavit of Substantial Hardship)

AL.name: Alabama Law Enforcement Agency (ALEA)
AL.what_they_offer: Provides official information, instructions, and the form required to obtain a certified criminal history record needed before filing for expungement, along with links to court petition forms.
AL.cost: $25 for the certified criminal history record

AL.name: Alabama Non-Violent Offenders (ANVO)
AL.what_they_offer: Helps non-violent offenders on a case-by-case basis to get Alabama or out-of-state arrest records expunged, apply for state pardons, and reinstate voting rights.

AL.name: Madison County Volunteer Lawyers
AL.what_they_offer: Listed in a directory of state-specific organizations providing free or low-cost criminal record clearing services.

AL.name: South Alabama Volunteer Lawyers
AL.what_they_offer: Listed in a directory of state-specific organizations providing free or low-cost criminal record clearing services.

AL.name: City of Birmingham Free Expungement Clinic
AL.what_they_offer: Hosts a free clinic with attorneys, court personnel, and partner legal groups to help residents clear eligible charges from their records by appointment.
AL.who_qualifies: Residents with eligible charges who complete a prescreen form in advance.

WA.name: King County Bar Association – The Records Project
WA.what_they_offer: Provides free legal representation to help residents vacate eligible criminal convictions in King County.
WA.who_qualifies: King County residents with incomes at or below 200% of the federal poverty level who have at least one eligible conviction in King County.

WA.name: Northwest Justice Project (CLEAR Line)
WA.what_they_offer: Helps people vacate past criminal convictions including Blake drug possession convictions, reduce or eliminate legal financial obligations, and restore driver's licenses. Operates the statewide CLEAR legal hotline for screening and referrals outside King County (in King County, callers dial 211).

WA.name: Civil Survival Project
WA.what_they_offer: Provides reentry legal advice, self-help guides, community clinics, and case-by-case representation to vacate eligible criminal convictions, clear Blake drug possession convictions, and reduce legal financial obligations.
WA.who_qualifies: Individuals with reentry-related legal needs resulting from prior involvement with the criminal legal system.

WA.name: Clark County Volunteer Lawyers Program
WA.what_they_offer: Offers one-on-one advising appointments and attorney paperwork support for self-represented individuals vacating records, with possible full representation on a case-by-case basis.

WA.name: Lavender Rights Project
WA.what_they_offer: Provides full legal representation to help clients vacate criminal records.
WA.who_qualifies: LGBTQ individuals seeking to vacate their criminal records.

WA.name: Tacomaprobono
WA.what_they_offer: Assists with civil legal matters including vacating records in Pierce County, with walk-in hours Monday through Thursday.
WA.who_qualifies: People who cannot afford to hire an attorney for a legal issue in Pierce County, regardless of where they live.

WA.name: Center for Justice
WA.what_they_offer: Offers low-cost legal assistance with vacating adult convictions and sealing records in the Spokane County court system.
WA.who_qualifies: Individuals seeking to clear adult convictions or seal records in Spokane County courts.
WA.cost: $200 for Vacate and Expungement Assistance and $200 for Sealing Assistance (vouchers, scholarships, and sliding scale available)

WA.name: Skagit Legal Aid
WA.area_served: Skagit, San Juan, Island, and Whatcom counties
WA.what_they_offer: Hosts rotating post-conviction clinics where volunteer attorneys review court records to check eligibility for vacating convictions and reducing or waiving legal financial obligations.
WA.who_qualifies: Anyone with convictions in Skagit, San Juan, or Island County (and Whatcom County under the state CRP partnership).

WA.name: Living with Conviction
WA.area_served: King, Pierce, Spokane, Clark, Cowlitz, and Wahkiakum counties
WA.what_they_offer: Provides legal information and post-conviction support regarding vacating drug possession charges, clearing eligible records, and addressing legal financial obligations.

WA.name: Gonzaga University School of Law – Juvenile Record Sealing Project
WA.what_they_offer: Helps eligible individuals seal juvenile court records in Spokane County.
WA.who_qualifies: People with eligible Spokane County juvenile records (excluding Rape 1, Rape 2, and Indecent Liberties with Forcible Compulsion) who have no open charges or active diversion, owe no restitution, and have completed the two- or five-year waiting period.

WA.name: Washington State Department of Commerce – Post-Conviction Legal Aid Program (CRP)
WA.what_they_offer: Funds regional legal aid and community partners across Washington (including Civil Survival, Skagit Legal Aid, Washington West African Center, Living with Conviction, Institute for Black Justice, Timberland Legal Aid, Seattle Clemency Project, and Washington Defender Association) to assist with vacating criminal records, reducing court fines, and restoring licenses.
WA.who_qualifies: People overcoming post-conviction barriers after involvement with the criminal legal system.

WA.name: Washington Courts
WA.what_they_offer: Publishes an informational guide explaining state laws and procedures for sealing and destroying juvenile and adult court records, vacating convictions, and deleting criminal history records.

WA.name: Washington State Patrol – Criminal History Records Section
WA.what_they_offer: Processes mail-in requests to delete eligible nonconviction arrest and charge records from Washington State Patrol criminal history files.
WA.who_qualifies: People with nonconviction records after two years from a favorable disposition or three years from arrest/citation, provided they have no prior felony or gross misdemeanor convictions, no intervening arrests or charges, and the case was not a deferred prosecution.

CT.name: Statewide Legal Services
CT.what_they_offer: Operates a central legal aid hotline and provides plain-language guides via CTLawHelp on Clean Slate, cannabis erasure, pardons, and juvenile records. Screens callers and routes eligible residents to regional legal aid offices when an erasable record causes a job or housing denial.
CT.who_qualifies: Income-qualifying Connecticut residents who pass legal aid financial screening.

CT.name: Greater Hartford Legal Aid Pardon Equity Project
CT.what_they_offer: Provides legal consultations to determine pardon eligibility and offers assistance with pardon applications, reachable by phone or at pardons@ghla.org.

CT.name: Connecticut Legal Services
CT.area_served: Throughout Connecticut except Greater Hartford and New Haven
CT.what_they_offer: Offers consultations with a lawyer to check pardon eligibility, assistance with pardon applications, and reentry legal guides.
CT.who_qualifies: Low-income Connecticut residents outside the Greater Hartford and New Haven areas.

CT.name: New Haven Legal Assistance Association
CT.what_they_offer: Provides legal screening and help with pardon applications as well as assistance when a conviction eligible for Clean Slate or cannabis erasure causes a housing or job denial.
CT.who_qualifies: Income-screened residents in the New Haven area, particularly those facing a housing or employment denial or deadline.

CT.name: New Haven Pardon Program
CT.what_they_offer: Provides hands-on assistance with completing Connecticut pardon applications via email at nhpardonprogram@gmail.com.

CT.name: Connecticut Pardon Team, Inc.
CT.what_they_offer: Provides non-legal information, tools, advice, and support to help individuals navigate the Board of Pardons and Paroles application process to seal or expunge convictions.
CT.who_qualifies: Individuals formerly convicted of a crime who have completed parole and/or probation and taken positive steps toward rehabilitation.

CT.name: Clean Slate Connecticut
CT.what_they_offer: Administers automatic record erasure for eligible post-2000 criminal and cannabis convictions and provides step-by-step instructions and court petition forms (Form JD-CR-202) for pre-2000 convictions.
CT.who_qualifies: Individuals with eligible misdemeanors or low-level felonies who have completed their sentences and remained conviction-free for seven or ten years, or those with qualifying cannabis convictions.
CT.cost: Zero court filing fees; fee applies for requesting an official criminal history record

CT.name: Connecticut Judicial Branch Law Libraries
CT.what_they_offer: Provides an online self-help portal with criminal case lookup tools, the Clean Slate erasure court petition form (Form JD-CR-202), erasure statutes, and links to legal aid guides.

OK.name: Oklahoma City University School of Law - HEROES Clinic
OK.area_served: Cleveland, Pottawatomie, Oklahoma, and Canadian Counties
OK.what_they_offer: Law students supervised by faculty and Legal Aid attorneys assess eligibility, draft expungement petitions, and represent clients to clear criminal records and waive court fines and fees.
OK.who_qualifies: Individuals whose arrests, charges, or convictions meet statutory expungement requirements, as well as people unable to pay outstanding court debt.

OK.name: Still She Rises, Tulsa
OK.what_they_offer: Provides holistic legal representation for expungement, criminal, municipal, parent defense, and court debt cases, and connects callers to other Tulsa legal resources when at capacity.

OK.name: Oklahoma State Bureau of Investigation (OSBI) - Clean Slate Initiative
OK.what_they_offer: Operates Oklahoma's Clean Slate process and Expedited Clean Slate Portal to clear eligible criminal history records without a court petition, and provides guidance on processing petition-based expungements.
OK.who_qualifies: Individuals with Clean Slate-eligible Oklahoma criminal records that contain final disposition information.
OK.cost: Court record expungement is free; arrest record expungement by petition has a $150 OSBI processing fee

OK.name: Urban League of Greater Oklahoma City Inc.
OK.what_they_offer: Hosts an annual Expungement Expo every June where applicants submit their OSBI report to be screened by volunteer attorneys for pro bono expungement representation.

OK.name: Criminal Justice and Mercy Ministries (CJAMM)
OK.what_they_offer: Assists with record-clearing eligibility assessments, document preparation, and court filing guidance, and connects individuals with legal professionals who handle expungement and record sealing.

OK.name: Oklahoma Indian Legal Services (OILS)
OK.what_they_offer: Provides legal assistance from attorneys on Native American legal matters, including criminal record expungement and sealing.

OK.name: Project Commutation (JusticeLink)
OK.what_they_offer: Provides an expungement attorney to help clients erase court records and clear OSBI background checks, alongside parole and commutation advocacy.

NV.name: Legal Aid Center of Southern Nevada
NV.what_they_offer: Provides free record sealing classes, forms, instructions, and one-on-one legal assistance through its Clean Slate Legal Assistance Program. Also helps eligible hotel and casino union workers and their families seal criminal records through the Culinary and Bartenders Unions Legal Service Fund Program.
NV.who_qualifies: Lower-income individuals with eligible records and no open cases or active warrants qualify, as do eligible Culinary Workers Union Local 226 and Bartenders Union Local 165 employees and their dependents.
NV.cost: Free legal services (court filing or application fees may apply)

NV.name: Nevada Legal Services
NV.what_they_offer: Offers weekly criminal record sealing classes in partnership with the UNLV William S. Boyd School of Law, along with self-help manuals. Also provides free legal advice and representation to help clients petition the court to seal past criminal records.
NV.who_qualifies: Community education classes are open to all, and legal advice and representation are available to eligible low-income Nevadans.

NV.name: UNLV William S. Boyd School of Law - Survivor Representation & Advocacy Clinic
NV.what_they_offer: Provides client-centered, trauma-informed legal representation for criminal record sealing, clemency, and pardon proceedings. Law students at the Boyd School of Law also teach free community classes on navigating the record sealing process in partnership with Nevada Legal Services.
NV.who_qualifies: Clinic representation is offered to people experiencing or at risk of experiencing traumatic violence, including intimate partner, gender-based, or state violence.

ND.name: Legal Services of North Dakota
ND.what_they_offer: Provides civil legal aid to eligible residents, including assistance or referrals for record sealing and reentry barriers, as well as screening for the Volunteer Lawyers program. They do not represent incarcerated people or handle criminal defense.
ND.who_qualifies: Low-income North Dakotans (generally at or below 125% of the federal poverty level) and seniors age 60 or older who are U.S. citizens or have proof of eligible immigration status.

ND.name: The F5 Project
ND.what_they_offer: Helps justice-impacted individuals navigate the record-sealing process and connects them with pro bono attorneys. They also offer reentry services including mentoring and employment support.
ND.who_qualifies: Justice-impacted individuals seeking reentry and record-sealing support.

ND.name: North Dakota Legal Self Help Center
ND.what_they_offer: Publishes legal research guides on expunging criminal records, sealing criminal records, and sealing DUI records, along with court fee waiver forms and an official form to close older nonconviction records. The center cannot provide forms for conviction sealing or direct help with criminal court processes.
ND.who_qualifies: Self-represented individuals researching North Dakota state court processes.

ND.name: North Dakota Supreme Court Law Library
ND.what_they_offer: Provides legal research guides and statutory references covering criminal record expungement, conviction sealing, and DUI record sealing in North Dakota.
ND.who_qualifies: Open to the judicial system, state agencies, bar members, and the public to the extent it does not compromise the library's primary purpose.

MI.name: Lakeshore Legal Aid
MI.what_they_offer: Provides legal assistance for expungements through scheduled clinics held across Macomb, Oakland, and Wayne Counties. Pre-registration is required to receive the clinic location and appointment time.
MI.who_qualifies: Residents of Macomb, Oakland, and Wayne Counties who meet Michigan's Clean Slate eligibility rules.

MI.name: University of Detroit Mercy School of Law Clinical Program
MI.area_served: Statewide, including Detroit and rural and tribal communities across the Upper and Lower Peninsulas
MI.what_they_offer: Law students, faculty, and volunteer attorneys run clinics and traveling expungement clinics to review Michigan criminal records, advise on eligibility, and help prepare applications to set aside convictions.
MI.who_qualifies: Individuals with eligible Michigan convictions under state waiting-period and felony-limit rules.

MI.name: Great Lakes Expungement Network (GLEN)
MI.what_they_offer: Offers full-service expungement help, including eligibility screenings, community clinics with fingerprinting and application guidance, and volunteer attorneys who handle filing and courtroom representation.

MI.name: Clean Slate GR (City of Grand Rapids)
MI.what_they_offer: Provides year-round assistance with filing expungements, along with attorney, notary, and fingerprinting services offered in collaboration with community partners.

MI.name: Safe & Just Michigan
MI.what_they_offer: Works with partner organizations, volunteer attorneys, and law students to host expungement fairs across Michigan that help people petition the courts to clear convictions.

MI.name: Legal Services of South Central Michigan (LSSCM)
MI.area_served: Barry, Branch, Calhoun, Clinton, Eaton, Hillsdale, Ingham, Jackson, Lenawee, Livingston, Monroe, Shiawassee, and Washtenaw Counties
MI.what_they_offer: Provides legal advice and representation for expungement cases, with intake available online or by phone through the Counsel & Advocacy Law Line.
MI.who_qualifies: Low-income individuals, families, and older adults in the 13 Michigan counties served.

MI.name: Legal Aid of Western Michigan
MI.area_served: Allegan, Berrien, Cass, Ionia, Kalamazoo, Kent, Lake, Mason, Mecosta, Montcalm, Muskegon, Newaygo, Oceana, Osceola, Ottawa, St. Joseph, and Van Buren Counties
MI.what_they_offer: Connects clients with volunteer attorneys for expungement cases through its Pro Bono Program and provides Clean Slate forms, checklists, and guides.

MI.name: Michigan Department of Attorney General - Expungement Assistance
MI.what_they_offer: Provides official Clean Slate eligibility information, step-by-step instructions for filing set-aside petitions without an attorney, and announcements of expungement fairs.

MI.name: Detroit Justice Center
MI.what_they_offer: Attorneys and Community Legal Advocates assist clients with record and traffic expungements, clearing warrants, and driver's license restoration.
MI.who_qualifies: Clients referred by partner organizations only; cannot assist with felonies, federal cases, out-of-state matters, or violent/assault misdemeanors.

KY.name: Legal Aid of the Bluegrass
KY.area_served: Anderson, Bath, Boone, Bourbon, Boyd, Boyle, Bracken, Campbell, Carroll, Carter, Elliott, Fayette, Fleming, Franklin, Gallatin, Grant, Greenup, Harrison, Jessamine, Kenton, Lewis, Mason, Menifee, Mercer, Montgomery, Morgan, Nicholas, Owen, Pendleton, Robertson, Rowan, Scott, and Woodford counties
KY.what_they_offer: Provides legal representation for criminal record expungements and partners with Goodwill of Kentucky and the City of Lexington to offer expungement clinics.
KY.who_qualifies: People living at or near poverty who need a Kentucky criminal record expunged to obtain or improve employment or overcome housing barriers.

KY.name: Legal Aid Society
KY.area_served: Breckinridge, Bullitt, Grayson, Hardin, Henry, Jefferson, Larue, Marion, Meade, Nelson, Oldham, Shelby, Spencer, Trimble, and Washington counties
KY.what_they_offer: Hosts group educational sessions and expungement clinics with Goodwill Kentucky where attorneys review background records, and refers complex cases to specialized divisions for legal representation.
KY.who_qualifies: Individuals with charges in the 15-county service area who qualify for Legal Aid Society services.

KY.name: AppalReD Legal Aid
KY.area_served: Adair, Bell, Breathitt, Casey, Clark, Clay, Clinton, Cumberland, Estill, Floyd, Garrard, Harlan, Jackson, Johnson, Knott, Knox, Laurel, Lawrence, Lincoln, Lee, Leslie, Letcher, Magoffin, Madison, Martin, McCreary, Monroe, Owsley, Perry, Pike, Powell, Pulaski, Rockcastle, Russell, Wayne, Whitley, and Wolfe counties
KY.what_they_offer: Participates in free expungement clinics where attorneys review background checks and advise on eligibility, and provides follow-up legal aid expungement services.
KY.who_qualifies: Participants with eligible criminal charges in its 37-county eastern and south-central Kentucky service area.

KY.name: Kentucky Legal Aid
KY.area_served: Allen, Ballard, Barren, Butler, Caldwell, Calloway, Carlisle, Christian, Crittenden, Daviess, Edmonson, Fulton, Graves, Green, Hancock, Hart, Henderson, Hickman, Hopkins, Livingston, Logan, Lyon, Marshall, McCracken, McLean, Metcalfe, Muhlenberg, Ohio, Simpson, Taylor, Todd, Trigg, Union, Warren, and Webster counties
KY.what_they_offer: Hosts free expungement clinics and provides attorneys to access and review criminal histories, check eligibility under Kentucky law, and help file expungement petitions.
KY.who_qualifies: Primarily serves low-income clients with criminal charges in its 35-county western and southern Kentucky service area.

KY.name: Goodwill Kentucky
KY.area_served: Statewide except Boone, Boyd, Caldwell, Campbell, Carter, Crittenden, Daviess, Greenup, Henderson, Hopkins, Kenton, Lawrence, Lewis, Martin, McLean, and Union counties
KY.what_they_offer: Partners with Kentucky civil legal aid programs to host in-person and virtual expungement clinics, obtains unofficial background records ahead of clinic appointments, and covers expungement costs within its coverage area.
KY.who_qualifies: People with eligible charges located within Goodwill Kentucky's covered counties.
KY.cost: Covers expungement costs within its service area

KY.name: Kentucky Justice Online (Legal Aid Network of Kentucky)
KY.what_they_offer: Provides free online self-help guides, instructions, and interactive guided interviews to prepare expungement petitions for acquittals, dismissed charges, or failure to indict.

KY.name: City of Lexington Clean Slate Expungement Clinic
KY.what_they_offer: Hosts quarterly expungement clinics offering one-on-one sessions with volunteer and legal aid attorneys to help start the expungement process.

KY.name: Louisville Urban League – Reily Reentry Project
KY.what_they_offer: Completes expungement paperwork and covers court and attorney fees to clear eligible criminal convictions.
KY.who_qualifies: Individuals with eligible Jefferson County convictions who enroll in any Louisville Urban League program.
KY.cost: Free (covers related court and attorney fees in exchange for program enrollment)

NY.name: Legal Services of Long Island – Sealing Clinic
NY.what_they_offer: Staff access, review, and verify RAP sheets to determine eligibility for criminal record sealing and other re-entry services.

NY.name: Community Service Society of New York – Next Door Project
NY.area_served: New York State (RAP sheet requests limited to the five boroughs of New York City)
NY.what_they_offer: Legal workers and attorneys request criminal records, correct RAP sheet errors, seal eligible cases, address open warrants, and apply for rehabilitation certificates.
NY.who_qualifies: Low-income New Yorkers with criminal records, with free record requests for those earning up to 200% of the federal poverty level.

NY.name: Legal Action Center (LAC)
NY.what_they_offer: Provides legal advice and representation to apply for New York record sealing, understand Clean Slate automatic sealing, get and fix RAP sheets, and apply for Certificates of Relief or Good Conduct.
NY.who_qualifies: New York State residents who have an arrest or conviction history.

NY.name: The Legal Aid Society – Case Closed Project
NY.what_they_offer: Provides direct legal representation and community education for criminal record sealing, expungement, and vacating convictions related to human trafficking.
NY.who_qualifies: Low-income individuals whose criminal convictions occurred in the five boroughs of New York City.

NY.name: Legal Aid Society of Northeastern New York
NY.area_served: Albany, Amsterdam, Canton, Gloversville, Plattsburgh, and Saratoga Springs
NY.what_they_offer: Handles New York criminal record sealing under CPL 160.59, applications for Certificates of Relief from Disabilities and Good Conduct, and employment or licensing denials.
NY.who_qualifies: People living in poverty who meet statutory sealing criteria, including having no more than two convictions and at least ten crime-free years.

NY.name: John Jay College Institute for Justice and Opportunity
NY.what_they_offer: Partners with a staff attorney to offer workshops and one-on-one legal help with sealing eligible convictions, requesting and fixing criminal records, and applying for rehabilitation certificates.
NY.who_qualifies: Institute program participants and current or prospective CUNY students and alumni with conviction records.

NY.name: Brooklyn Defender Services (BDS)
NY.what_they_offer: Helps clients seal eligible arrest records and provides reentry support and civil legal advocacy around employment, housing, and education.
NY.who_qualifies: Low-income Brooklyn residents and Brooklyn Defenders' clients who are legally entitled to record sealing.

NY.name: Legal Assistance of Western New York (LawNY) – Clean Slate Act help
NY.what_they_offer: Free civil legal aid from 7 offices serving 14 Western New York counties. Its Clean Slate Act page explains which New York records are sealed automatically and when, and you can apply for help online.

MS.name: Mississippi Center for Justice
MS.what_they_offer: Helps individuals gather court and arrest documents, drafts expungement petitions, orders, and fee-waiver motions for self-represented filing, and hosts expungement clinics. Acceptance of new online eligibility forms is temporarily paused while staff assist people already on the waitlist.
MS.who_qualifies: Anyone seeking to clear an eligible arrest, misdemeanor, or felony from their Mississippi record, including individuals experiencing financial hardship.

MS.name: Mississippi Volunteer Lawyers Project
MS.what_they_offer: Hosts self-representation legal clinics where volunteer attorneys provide legal advice, drafted pleadings, and court instructions for felony and misdemeanor expungements. Also offers an online expungement workshop and video.
MS.who_qualifies: Low- to moderate-income residents with income at or below 200% of the federal poverty level who bring required court records.

MS.name: Mission First Legal Aid Office
MS.what_they_offer: Provides free civil legal assistance on a range of legal matters, including criminal record expungement.
MS.who_qualifies: Eligible residents in Hinds, Madison, and Rankin Counties.

MS.name: Mississippi Access to Justice Commission
MS.what_they_offer: Provides self-help information on Mississippi expungement law and supports ExpungeMississippi.com with the Magnolia Bar Association to help users check eligibility, find free legal aid providers, and locate upcoming expungement clinics.
MS.who_qualifies: People who are handling their legal problems without a lawyer.

AK.name: Alaska Legal Services Corporation
AK.what_they_offer: Provides free civil legal aid across Alaska, including assistance with criminal record clearing, driver license restoration, and other reentry barriers. People seeking help can apply online, in person at local offices, or through a statewide toll-free intake phone line.
AK.who_qualifies: Low-income and vulnerable Alaskans, generally those with incomes at or below 125% of the federal poverty level (or up to 200% for certain case types).
